articles.summary: Scotland head coach Mel Andreatta on Scotland, Sweden and chasing her World Cup dream.
articles.body:
Radio Scotland , · 21 Nov 2026 , · 25 mins

Mel Andreatta sits down with Jane Lewis to discuss life on and off the pitch ahead of Scotland’s huge World Cup play-off with Sweden. How has the Australian made Ayrshire feel like home, and what has she learned since taking charge of the national team? She reveals the messages exchanged with former colleague Tony Gustavsson before they meet in opposite dugouts and explains why Scotland won’t be intimidated by Sweden’s reputation. articles.title: Made tactical mistakes, erred, but risks are must for India to progress: Jamil
articles.summary: Panaji: The stats don’t lie.
articles.body: Panaji: The stats don’t lie.Khalid Jamil has been in this business for over 15 years and needs no reminding that a coach gets judged by the results he obtains. His record with the national team isn’t encouraging. Two wins from 17 matches, five draws, for a 12% winning rate and 0.7 points per match.Jamil’s first win came in Jamil’s first game as national team coach, against Tajikistan. It was a wonderful start but 2026 saw the team notch just one win, in an inconsequential tie against lower-ranked Hong Kong.“As a coach, I’ve erred, made mistakes tactically, but I’ve taken risks too which were a must at this stage,” the India coach told TOI after the conclusion of the two international friendlies in New Zealand last week. “For example, I had two choices: play these friendlies against New Zealand, a World Cup team, or go to SAFF Championship, where India are the highest ranked (team). If I wanted to play it safe, I could have gone with the team to Bangladesh and improved the (winning) statistics.”India have now lost four matches in a row, all against teams that featured at the last FIFA World Cup. Jamil’s side conceded 19 goals in five friendlies during the last two windows and scored twice, which included an encouraging 1-1 draw against Panama.“We were good against Panama, played brilliantly, could have even won. We dominated. Everyone was praising us. Now, everyone is saying we are miserable. The criticism is not good for the players. I’ve told them to stay strong mentally since they can get affected by all this negativity,” said Jamil.The coach himself has not been spared. He says he can handle the heat, though “criticism on social media based on religion is not good.” His selection policy is straightforward: “everybody is the same for me; perform and get into the team.”Since being appointed in August 2025, Jamil, 49, has handed debuts to 18 players, the most by any national team coach in his first year in-charge. Yet, despite the constant chopping and changing, India still does not wear a settled look. In fact, against New Zealand he fielded Ashique Kuruniyan, a winger, in midfield, while the position of centre-backs was also changed.“It’s not as if I took the centre-backs and played them as forwards,” shot back Jamil.“Ashique was needed in midfield because of his physicality. If you see the second half against New Zealand (which ended goalless), we played well. The best part is that we had five debutants in that half and I was impressed with the players. Hrithik (Tiwari) in goal, Tomba (Singh), (Lalrinliana) Hnamte, David (Lalhlansanga), (Muhammad) Suhail too.”Jamil feels India’s performances have to be seen from a different lens. Clubs refusing to release players, injuries to regulars (Anwar, Apuia, Sahal for NZ friendlies), different time zones, hectic travel and limited training sessions.“You cannot go into games blindly (without preparations). New Zealand was a big lesson for us,” said Jamil. “Without preparations, it’s not easy to play. Yes, it’s true that I have tried many players, made changes, experimented, because I want to find the best team. I accept the results were not good. But without risks (of playing much higher-ranked opponents), we cannot improve.“You have to be patient. You have to trust. I am not someone who will put his hands up (and quit). I will fight, 100%, for the country. I will complete the job.”Jamil signed a two-year contract in August last year with an assurance that he will have an uninterrupted run.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: College football winners and losers: Big Ten's dismal day could doom conference's playoff hopes
articles.summary: Could the Big Ten only really get one school in the 12-team field?
articles.body:
The Big Ten's nightmare playoff scenario is here.

The chances of the conference getting only one team into the College Football Playoff increased significantly in Week 12 as No. 4 UCLA lost in triple-overtime to Michigan , No. 8 Indiana dropped its second game of the season in an overtime loss at Washington and No. 14 Ohio State's season descended into further misery with a loss at Nebraska.

UCLA's undefeated season ended with the loss to the Wolverines, but the Bruins suffered a potentially much more significant blow on the first play of overtime when QB Ty Dieffenbach got tackled to the ground. The Bruins' starter stayed down after the play and had to be carted off the field on a stretcher after trainers tended to him.

Dieffenbach was replaced by Madden Iamaleava, who looked very much like a quarterback who started the season No. 3 on the team's depth chart. Iamaleava — whose brother Nico suffered a season-ending knee injury in UCLA's win over Oregon — is in line to start against No. 18 USC in Week 13 presuming that Dieffenbach is unable to play.

For now, UCLA should stay in the provisional College Football Playoff field in Tuesday's rankings. The same can't be said for Indiana, which could drop out of the top 11 and is also now in a three-way tie with Oregon and Iowa for second place in the Big Ten.

The Hoosiers could be on the wrong side of the tiebreaker, too.

The Big Ten's primary tiebreaker for ties among teams that haven't played each other is record against common opponents. All three teams beat Northwestern and Michigan. Iowa beat Washington. And Oregon has Washington next week. A win there knocks Indiana out of the Big Ten title game in a three-way tie.

The four-way tie is also in play. UCLA is now 7-1 in conference play and would fall to 7-2 with a loss to USC next week.

We won't go further into tiebreaker minutiae for now, but you get the point. The top of the Big Ten could be an abject mess. That isn't good for the conference's playoff hopes.

If Dieffenbach is out for the season, UCLA drops to 10-2 and is on the wrong side of the Big Ten's title-game tiebreakers, will the committee drop the Bruins out of the playoff? It's not a scenario that's exactly like Florida State's in 2023, but there's at least a precedent for the committee to drop a team that looks worse with a backup quarterback.

In a world where a two-loss UCLA isn't in as an at-large, what's the argument for the three-loss loser of the Big Ten title game to get in the field if BYU finishes the season at 10-2 and either Wake Forest or Miami is 11-2?

The Big Ten has boasted the last three national champions thanks to elite teams at the top of a conference that didn't have elite depth. This year, the Big Ten's depth might have improved, but it's come at the detriment of the top of the conference. Not one team looks capable of winning the national title.

Here are the rest of this week's winners and losers:

Wake Forest: On a day the Big Ten's top teams struggled, Wake Forest showed why it shouldn't be an afterthought for the playoff. The Demon Deacons outscored Georgia Tech 36-7 in the first half of a 50-29 win. Georgia Tech's first-half touchdown was the first time a team had scored against Wake Forest in the first half since NC State over a month ago. QB Gio Lopez was 17-of-22 passing for 324 yards and two touchdowns, while Deuce Lawrence rushed 13 times for 105 yards and Ty Clark III had 18 carries for 98 yards. The Demon Deacons should be a playoff lock with a win over Duke in Week 13.

Clemson: Say whatever you want about Dabo Swinney and the way that he's handled Clemson's struggles for a second straight season . But Friday night was clear that his team has not quit on the season. Down to No. 3 QB Trent Pearman, the Tigers kept star Duke running back Nate Sheppard to 116 yards on 19 carries and Blue Devils QB Walker Eget threw 38 times for just 149 yards. It wasn't a pretty win — WR Bryant Wesco threw an interception and the Tigers rushed the ball 51 times — but Clemson is now assured of a winning season.

Houston QB Keisean Henderson: The highly touted freshman made the first start of his career at West Virginia on Saturday and led the No. 20 Cougars to a 34-31 win at West Virginia. Starting in place of Conner Weigman, Henderson was 18-of-28 passing for 268 yards and a TD while rushing 14 times for 39 yards. Houston's chances of making the playoff were zapped in Week 11 with a loss at Colorado. But a 10-win season is still in play with a win over Baylor to end the regular season and a bowl victory.

Tulane: The 2026 season has been a poor sequel to last season's College Football Playoff blockbuster. But Will Hall's team got a massive win over North Texas on Saturday. The Green Wave won 28-24 after falling behind 14-0 in the first quarter. QB Trace Johnson was 17-of-21 passing for 283 yards and four touchdowns, while WR Cameron Roberts had four grabs for 81 yards and two TDs. The win also made Tulane bowl eligible and it might have taken North Texas out of the American Conference title game.

Florida State: Rick Stockstill's record as FSU's interim coach is now 2-1. The Seminoles lost 28-10 at home to NC State — a team also led by an interim coach after Dave Doeren's firing — in an absolutely ugly second-half performance. NC State scored three straight touchdowns in the final 30 minutes to turn a 10-7 halftime deficit into an 18-point win. QB Ashton Daniels threw two interceptions as the Seminoles dropped to 5-6. A win over Florida is necessary for a bowl game.

Massachusetts : It was set up so perfectly for the Minutemen in Week 12. UMass entered the penultimate week of the season simply needing a win over a 1-9 Akron team to get to six wins and bowl eligibility for the first time. Instead, Akron got a 34-33 road win. UMass allowed 379 yards on just 52 plays and was outscored 17-7 in the second half. Bowling Green (3-8) is up in Week 13. Can UMass beat the Falcons to get to the postseason?

Colorado: The Buffaloes' dream of a bowl game has ended. Colorado turned the ball over four times in a 35-28 road loss to Cincinnati. Isaac Wilson threw three picks and Quanell Farrakhan Jr. lost a fumble. The Buffs had the ball twice in the fourth quarter, but turned the ball over on downs and then Wilson threw his final interception of the game with 40 seconds to go. The loss dropped Colorado to 4-7 ahead of their final game of the season against UCF.

South Florida: Brian Hartline's first season in charge in Tampa has been rough. The Bulls are bowl eligible at 6-5 but fell to 2-5 in the American with a 35-14 loss at Florida Atlantic on Saturday. The loss was USF's third in a row as they fell to just one game above last place in the American. USF rushed 27 times for just 45 yards and has Tulane in Week 13.

articles.title: Barcelona talent Hafiz Gariba hit by injury setback
articles.summary: The teenager has a hamstring problem.
articles.body:
Barcelona Atletic boss Juliano Belletti has suffered yet another injury blow as exciting young defender Hafiz Gariba has become the latest player to be sidelined.

The teenager sustained a hamstring problem in Barca Atletic's defeat to Girona last time out and is now set for some time out of action.

"Player Hafiz Gariba reported discomfort after the match against Girona B. Medical tests have confirmed a hamstring injury in his left leg, similar to those suffered by Dani Ávila, Diarra and Onstein. The estimated recovery time is 5 to 7 weeks," he added.

The defender joins Dani Ávila, Ibrahim Diarra and Juwensley Onstein in being sidelined as a result of the Girona game. Belletti had hoped the match wouldn't go ahead, as he was short of players due to injuries and international commitments, but his team were forced to play and are still counting the cost.

The international break has also brought another injury blow, with Barca also confirming that Josue Caicedo is out for four weeks with a hamstring problem following his return from the national team.

Hafiz Gariba is a player who has been tipped to break into the first team at Barcelona and has earned rave reviews already this season . Let's hope he – and his fellow Barca Atletic team-mates – recover well and are back in action soon.

articles.title: Adrian Peterson Jr. Lands CFB Offer from Oklahoma amid Miami, FSU, Texas Tech Interest
articles.summary: Adrian Peterson Jr., the son of former star NFL running back Adrian Peterson, could be considering attending his father's alma mater.
articles.body:
Adrian Peterson Jr., the son of former star NFL running back Adrian Peterson, could be considering attending his father's alma mater.

The Class of 2030 athlete has received an offer from Oklahoma, he announced Saturday on social media.

Biggest 5-Star Recruiting Busts of Past Decade 👎

Peterson has also received offers from programs including Miami, Florida State, Texas Tech and Texas A&M, according to 247Sports .

He also holds offers from Baylor, Minnesota, Oklahoma, Syracuse, TCU, SMU, UTSA, Missouri State and Texas State, 247Sports reported.

Peterson, listed at 6'1" and 175 pounds, is a freshman at Fort Bend Ridge Point High School in Missouri City, Texas.

He entered the program as a wide receiver, running back and defensive back, per KPRC 2's Aaron Wilson .

Peterson has so far recorded seven catches for 95 yards and two touchdowns in six games, according to MaxPreps .

Peterson told Wilson Oklahoma was "definitely one of my favorite colleges" as of last May.

"He doesn't really care," Peterson said about his father's input in his eventual college decision. "It's mostly about where I want to go and where I feel like the coaching staff is the best and who I have a relationship with the most."

Peterson Sr. racked up 4,041 rushing yards and finished as runner-up for the Heisman Trophy while playing for the Sooners from 2004 to 2006.

"Yeah," Peterson Sr. recently told Oklahoma Daily Sports when asked if he wanted to see his son join the Sooners. "He's been waiting for this opportunity, so I'm pretty excited for him."

Peterson's father ranks fifth all-time among NFL running backs with 14,918 career rushing yards over 15 seasons. Scouts around the NCAA will be watching to see if Peterson continues showing potential of similar talent as his high school career progresses.

articles.title: Kansas City Current win their first NWSL championship, defeating the Washington Spirit 2-1
articles.summary: WASHINGTON — Vanessa DiBernardo scored directly off a corner kick in the 54th minute to lift the Kansas City Current to their first championship in the National Women’s Soccer League, 2-1 over the Washington Spirit on Saturday night.
articles.body: WASHINGTON — Vanessa DiBernardo scored directly off a corner kick in the 54th minute to lift the Kansas City Current to their first championship in the National Women’s Soccer League, 2-1 over the Washington Spirit on Saturday night. Debinha added an insurance goal deep into stoppage time, and the Current needed it when Trinity Rodman scored for Washington in the 98th minute. Kansas City held on through a couple more tense scrambles in front to claim the title. DiBernardo sent a corner in from the left side early in the second half, and the ball curled into the net as Kansas City’s Kayla Sharples and Washington goalkeeper Sandy MacIver both jumped for it. Spirit players appealed for a foul on Sharples, but the goal stood. The rare Olympic goal — the term for a corner kick that goes directly into the net without another player redirecting it — delivering the championship to the Current in their sixth season of existence. Washington, the league’s 2021 champion, has lost in the final the last three seasons. This time the game was played at Audi Field, the Spirit’s home stadium. Not even the crowd at “Rowdy Audi” could deny Kansas City. The Current dominated the league during a record-setting regular season last year, only to be eliminated in their postseason opener. This year they were the No. 4 seed, but beat top-seeded Gotham FC and Washington in the semifinals and final. Kansas City’s Laney Rouse crashed into Rodman from behind in the fifth minute, leaving the Washington star shaken up. Rodman was quickly able to return but spent considerable time stretching out her left arm before becoming a bigger factor in the game near the end of the first half. The best chance of the opening 45 minutes came shortly after Rodman’s injury. Temwa Chawinga came in alone from the left, but the angle wasn’t the best and Spirit goalkeeper Sandy MacIver was able to make the save. Washington tried to increase the pressure after DiBernardo gave the Current the lead. Rodman made a lengthy run and set up Clara Luvanga, but her left-footed shot went wide in the 72nd minute. A couple minutes later, Kansas City goalie Lorena went diving to her right to keep out Tara Rudd’s header off a corner. MacIver made another big save on Chawinga in the 85th minute, coming out of the penalty area to cut down the angle. Moments later at the other end, Lorena came out to contest a high ball and collided with Rodman. Both players remained down for a while before playing on. The crowd received a boost with the addition of nine minutes of stoppage, and Washington received a free kick just outside the penalty area. But the Kansas City wall held firm, and Debinha came back the other way. She had Chawinga to her left, but instead dribbled around MacIver to the right and put the Current up 2-0.

articles.title: NWSL championship: Current win first title as Spirit fall in third straight final
articles.summary: Despite a late goal to get back within one, Washington's heartbreak continues with a 2-1 loss to Kansas City.
articles.body: For the first time in franchise history, the Kansas City Current are NWSL champions. The Current defeated the Washington Spirit 2-1 in Saturday's final, denying Washington a trophy yet again.The Spirit entered this game with momentum, talent and a home-field advantage at Audi Field in Washington, D.C.. And yet, once again, they are ending the season without a trophy, after falling in their third straight NWSL final.In the chippy first half, neither team was able to get much going on offense, though both teams picked up plenty of fouls: The Spirit and Current were called for 19 fouls combined in the first half. That number ended at 35 total fouls, near-evenly split between the two teams, as evidence of the physical match.Star Washington forward Trinity Rodman went through an early injury scare, landing hard on her shoulder after a tackle from rookie defender Laney Rouse. Rodman stayed down for a while in obvious pain, but returned to the game after being tended to by trainers. After presumably receiving treatment at halftime, Rodman continued to play with significant tape on her left shoulder.With both teams unable to create offensive structure, set pieces became crucial opportunities to break through. In the 54th minute, Vanessa DiBernardo pulled the Current ahead with an Olimpico goal, scoring a curving shot from the corner to quiet the rowdy Audi crowd.VANESSA DIBERNARDO CHAMPIONSHIP OLIMPICO ‼️2026 NWSL Championship pres. by Google Pixel pic.twitter.com/3s7gxACgGr— National Women’s Soccer League (@NWSL) November 22, 2026 Kansas City padded its score in the seventh minute of stoppage time, as Debinha broke away for an easy, uncontested goal off a counterattack.Debinha tricks the keeper and IN ‼️2026 NWSL Championship pres. by Google Pixel pic.twitter.com/3Rhghyx2iu— National Women’s Soccer League (@NWSL) November 22, 2026 That turned out to be a good thing for the Current: One minute later, Rodman got a header off a set piece that deflected off a KC defender and into the goal.Minutes left and Trinity Rodman gets the Spirit on the board 👊2026 NWSL Championship pres. by Google Pixel pic.twitter.com/pljM6Dn3gu— National Women’s Soccer League (@NWSL) November 22, 2026 The goal gave Washington just a little bit of hope to close the final gap, but it didn't end up being enough to overcome that Kansas City lead.DiBernardo, who returned to the Current in July after missing a year on maternity leave, was named MVP for the Final. At 34, DiBernardo became the oldest player to score in the championship game, and celebrated with her baby after the match. The victory was a long-awaited pinnacle for the Current, who avenge last year's historic Shield win-turned-stunning first-round exit. Just five years after the franchise's creation, Kansas City lifted the NWSL trophy, dashing the Spirit's dreams in the process.

articles.title: Where Should South Carolina Be Ranked in CFP Poll After Loss to Georgia?
articles.summary: The No. 1 Georgia Bulldogs punched their ticket to the SEC championship game with a 34-6 victory over the No. 21 South Carolina Gamecocks on Saturday night.
articles.body:
The No. 1 Georgia Bulldogs punched their ticket to the SEC championship game with a 34-6 victory over the No. 21 South Carolina Gamecocks on Saturday night.

The Bulldogs have sat atop the College Football Playoff rankings for two consecutive weeks, and they'll likely continue to hold onto that spot after another dominant outing against a ranked opponent.

Georgia's last time at the No. 1 spot was short-lived. The Bulldogs suffered a 27-24 loss to unranked Auburn right after they had climbed to the top. Since then, they have dominated their opponents in lopsided wins. The Bulldogs entered Saturday's game on a three-game win streak, outscoring their opponents by a combined 81 points during that span.

Major Big Ten Upsets Change Our Top 25 ↕️

The Gamecocks picked up their fifth loss of the season, which will likely drop them out of the CFP rankings. Despite what the score indicates, South Carolina still put together an admirable performance. Georgia entered the game as 14.5-point favorites on FanDuel Sportsbook , but South Carolina kept the game competitive throughout the first half.

Here's a look at the top performers from both teams:

South Carolina became the first team this season to score first against Georgia, and just the third team to score on Georgia's defense in the first quarter. The Gamecocks put together two impressive drives to open the game, but they stalled out in the red zone and were held to a pair of field goals.

The Gamecocks led for most of the first half, but their inability to capitalize in the red zone would prove to be costly. They held Georgia's offense to just three points on their first two possessions, but the Bulldogs managed to pull ahead late in the second quarter.

Georgia running back Nate Frazier scored the first touchdown of the game on a 1-yard run in the final two minutes of the half.

The Bulldogs went into halftime holding a slim 10-7 lead, but they managed to pull away in the third quarter. Frazier capped off Georgia's 5-play, 75-yard opening drive of the second half with a 2-yard rushing touchdown, his second of the game.

The 17-6 lead evidently wasn't enough for Georgia coach Kirby Smart, who did his best Sean Payton impression and pulled off a surprise onside kick to steal a possession from South Carolina.

The Gamecocks managed to hold the Bulldogs scoreless with a three-and-out, but their offense failed to muster a first down of their own on the following possession.

Georgia's special teams unit came up with another big play and returned the punt for 48 yards. The Bulldogs offense began their next drive at South Carolina's 21-yard line, but they were forced to settle for kicker Peyton Woodring's 40-yard field goal after being stifled by the Gamecocks defense once again.

The Gamecocks put together an impressive 11-play, 53-yard drive to get to the edge of the red zone, but Georgia forced the game's first turnover with Walker intercepting LaNorris Sellers at the 9-yard line.

Georgia put the game out of reach early in the fourth quarter with a 14-yard touchdown on an end-around to wide receiver Craig Dandridge. Then, running back Nick Peal added on another score for good measure.

During his postgame interview on the field, Smart said he preached "patience" to his team throughout the game.

Georgia improved to 10-1 overall with an 8-1 SEC record. The Bulldogs have won double-digit games every season since 2021, tied for the second-most consecutive 10-win seasons in SEC history.

Georgia will face the Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets in their regular-season finale next Saturday.

articles.title: Kang-in, un lujo asiático
articles.standfirst: Coronado otra vez como el mejor del continente, está llamado a marcar diferencias ante su rival fetiche
articles.summary: Coronado otra vez como el mejor del continente, está llamado a marcar diferencias ante su rival fetiche
articles.body: Aunque el trasiego internacional apunta a relegarle a la suplencia, Kang-in Lee regresa al Atlético erigido en un verdadero lujo asiático. Se mire por donde se mire: por el reconocimiento que le confirma como el mayor icono de su continente, por el encaje en el ataque rojiblanco y por su tendencia a dejar huella frente al Getafe. De ahí que, presumiblemente durante la segunda mitad, está llamado a marcar diferencias en el Coliseum agarrado a una zurda con potencial como para disparar sus cifras. Si el año pasado ya emuló a un mito nacional como Park al convertirse en el segundo surcoreano en levantar la Champions, ahora acaba de confirmar el sorpasso a Son como el futbolista con más tirón más allá del continente, siendo el primero que repite como Mejor jugador asiático en el fútbol internacional de 2026, galardón que el ex del Tottenham conquistó en cuatro ocasiones, pero nunca consecutivas. De hecho, ni las buenas prestaciones de su compatriota Hwang In-beom en el Oporto ni del japonés Ueda, en el Lille y el Feyenoord, han sido suficientes como para desbancar a Kang in como máximo icono oriental. Una fama granjeada durante sus tres temporadas como recambio del elenco de estrellas del PSG y ahora apunta a incrementarse con su papel más protagonista en el Atlético por más que hasta ahora haya dejado mejores sensaciones que números. En este sentido, pese a estrenarse como rojiblanco con un zurdazo por la escuadra del Málaga, sus dos únicas dianas (también marcó a Osasuna con un derechazo desde el interior del área) no hacen justicia a lo que genera en las inmediaciones del área, bien en la asociación, en el regate o en los cambios de orientación que dejó en el último partido frente al Barcelona, como con un disparo marca de la casa al que los palos o el caudal de intentos aún no han permitido traducirlo en una mayor producción anotadora. Aunque en su explosión en LaLiga anterior a su fichaje por el PSG, Kang in se caracterizó más por su desequilibrio por sus goles, tres de los diez que firmó con las camisetas del Valencia (3) y el Mallorca (7) fueron precisamente frente al Getafe, que junto al Angers y el Montpellier pasa por ser el equipo más castigado por el surcoreano. Cierto es que también es al que más veces se ha enfrentado (10), pero ahora con una amenaza añadida: el posicionamiento por los carriles interiores y más cerca del área desde donde Simeone pretende destapar su vena goleadora.

articles.title: La Liga del Atlético se ‘gana’ a domicilio
articles.standfirst: Simeone calca el arranque como visitante del año del primer título y supera en dos puntos el del último. Con otra victoria firmaría el mejor inicio tras las primeras siete salidas
articles.summary: Simeone calca el arranque como visitante del año del primer título y supera en dos puntos el del último. Con otra victoria firmaría el mejor inicio tras las primeras siete salidas
articles.body: El Atlético regresa a cinco puntos del líder de un parón al que se habría ido en lo más alto de la tabla de haber vencido en su último partido en el Metropolitano frente al Barcelona. Sin embargo, más allá de los duelos directos frente a los dos grandes (al Real Madrid sí le derrotó ante su afición), lo que determinará si los de Simeone se mantienen en la pelea por el título será su rendimiento como visitantes. Así sucedió en las dos ocasiones en las que El Cholo se coronó campeón, mostrando desde el inicio un puño de hierro... que ha sido recuperado e incluso fortalecido en este curso. Si las dificultades para mantener la regularidad a domicilio y los tropiezos en estadios de equipos de la zona media o baja han lastrado las posibilidades del Atlético de luchar por el campeonato en los mismos curso, las seis primeras salidas del presente ejercicio permiten a los rojiblancos seguir mirando a los ojos a los dos grandes transatlánticos españoles. Nada que ver con los precedentes en los que las distancias abiertas en los primeros meses obligaban a seguir el camino a contrarreloj. Tanto es así que tras las cinco victorias cosechadas en el Sánchez Pizjuán (1-3), Anoeta (0-3), Mendizorroza (1-2), RCDE Stadium (0-1) y Ciutat de Valencia (0-2) y la única derrota en San Mamés (3-0), el Atlético calca los mismos 15 puntos sumados en los primeros seis desplazamientos de la inolvidable temporada 13-14 en la que Simeone acabó levantando una Liga que no se celebraba desde el Doblete de 1996. Un arranque incluso mejor que el de la última vez en la que El Cholo lo volvió a hacer y arrebató el título a Real Madrid y Barcelona, pues el balance a estas alturas era de cuatro victorias, un empate y una derrota que sumaban 13 puntos lejos del Metropolitano. Señales inequívocas ambas de que el Atlético marcha por el buen camino para competir en lo más alto. Paradójicamente, aún hay una campaña en la actual gloriosa época de la mano del técnico en la que el Atlético arrancó más intratable como foráneo, firmando cinco triunfos y una igualada. Sin embargo, aquella 22-23 tuvo la anomalía de que por entonces también había caído dos veces y había concedido un empate en su feudo. Una irregularidad que si bien alejaría el título, no impediría a los de Simeone acabar a un solo punto del eterno rival que sería segundo. La otra gran excepción se encuentra en el curso 18-19, pues a pesar de firmar el peor arranque del Cholo a domicilio con siete puntos (un triunfo, cuatro empates y una derrota), el Atlético acabaría alcanzando la velocidad de crucero hasta acabar subcampeón. Una remontada convertida en norma desde que Simeone acudió al rescate tras la desesperada llamada de Gil Marín, pues pese a que Manzano había arrancado con un único punto en sus seis primeras citas lejos del Calderón, el curso 11-12 acabaría en Europa (título continental incluido). Hoy, la victoria en el Coliseum esconde el mejor inicio fuera de casa jamás visto, pues tras caer el Atlético en Cádiz en su séptimo desplazamiento de la 22-23 y empatar en Villarreal en la 13-14, los 18 puntos de 21 a los que se irían los de Simeone superarían el récord de 16.

articles.title: Francho Serrano: "El fútbol pone pequeñas trabas a sus mejores guerreros"
articles.standfirst: El futbolista azulón analiza en Marca el partido frente al Atlético de Madrid
articles.summary: El futbolista azulón analiza en Marca el partido frente al Atlético de Madrid
articles.body: Francho Serrano (7 de octubre de 2001) llegó este verano a Getafe después de un salto que lo llevó de Segunda División el curso pasado y de hacer pretemporada en 1.ª RFEF a jugar en Conference League de la noche a la mañana. El mediocentro se ha adaptado a la perfección al estilo de un equipo, el azulón, que debe mejorar sus prestaciones para lograr los objetivos marcados. En la previa del partido frente al Atlético de Madrid, el zaragozano analiza el choque frente a los de Simeone, en un duelo en el que vivirá varios reencuentros especiales de su época en un Real Zaragoza al que sigue viendo y alentando desde la capital. PREGUNTA. ¿Cómo te encuentras después del parón? RESPUESTA. Con ganas, con muchas ganas de volver a competir, que es para lo que nosotros trabajamos y disfrutamos del fútbol: para competir y para dar alegrías a la gente. Qué mejor partido que uno contra uno de los mejores equipos del campeonato y ahora mismo de Europa y del mundo, que es el Atlético de Madrid. P. Los parones dan un poco de rabia, sobre todo cuando vienes después de la derrota, ¿se ha hecho largo? R. Sí, porque tienes ganas de volver a ganar, de que llegue cuanto antes el partido siguiente para cambiar la dinámica. Ha tocado vivirlo con un parón de por medio. También ha sido bueno para recargar pilas, desconectar un poco que también es importante en muchos momentos. Tenemos ganas de que llegue ya el fin de semana. Estamos en casa y sabemos que va a ser un partido súper complicado, en el que vamos a tener que estar no al 100, sino al 150 % durante todo el encuentro, porque ellos ahora mismo son muy determinantes y, como no estemos dando ese porcentaje de nivel, va a ser un partido muy complicado. P. ¿Es el mejor momento para enfrentaros al Atleti tras el parón? R. Contra estos equipos nunca sabes cuándo es bueno jugar, porque tienen plantillas tan grandes y tan amplias que, como yo siempre digo, tienen equipo A y equipo B, pero cualquiera de los dos puede ser titular perfectamente. Nunca sabes cuándo es el momento para cogerles. Lo importante es centrarnos en nosotros, en lo que depende de nosotros, que es hacer un buen partido, estar ordenados, esperar nuestro momento y trabajar desde el orden defensivo, que es lo que caracteriza siempre al Getafe, y a partir de ahí crecer. P. ¿En quién te fijas en el Atlético de Madrid? R. En muchos. Yo, sobre todo ahora por cercanía de edad, por posición y por todo, obviamente me fijo en Pablo Barrios. Creo que es un chico que ha tenido un crecimiento exponencial en los últimos años, ha llegado a la selección absoluta y tiene el techo todavía muchísimo más alto. Ojalá algún día podamos coincidir porque creo que además haríamos buenas migas. También me fijo mucho en Giuliano porque estuvimos juntos en Zaragoza, le guardo mucho cariño, hemos mantenido la relación y me alegro de todo lo bien que le está yendo porque se lo merece, se lo ha currado como nadie. También es una alegría poder verle el fin de semana. P. Y además tiene el doble mérito después de la grave lesión que sufrió, un poco parecido a lo que le pasó a Uche. R. Sí. Cuando le pasó, obviamente, estaba súper dolido porque su oportunidad de llegar al fútbol profesional, a Primera División con el Alavés, le hacía muchísima ilusión. Te llega un batacazo como ese, una lesión tan grave, y nunca sabes cuándo tienes que pasar por quirófano, cómo vas a salir ni cómo vas a volver. Pero un chico como él, con lo disciplinado que es y con las ganas que tiene de generar su propia historia por sí mismo, está demostrando mucho. El año pasado, si no me equivoco, jugó 60 partidos en el Atlético de Madrid. Eso no se lo regala nadie. Está en la selección absoluta argentina y eso dice mucho, no solo de él como jugador, sino también como profesional. P. Además, también tiene que pelear con eso de ser ‘hijo de’, porque el día que haces un mal partido es el que juega por decreto. R. Sí, correcto. Pero, como te digo, yo que lo conozco, él siempre ha querido tener su nombre, hacerse su nombre. Creo que cada día hay menos gente que puede achacarle eso porque, por el trabajo y por el profesional que es, está demostrando que se merece y mucho estar donde está. P. Acabo de caer en que también coincidiste el año pasado con Gabi, le puedes pegar un toque para que te eche una mano… R. Gabi siempre ha sido, sobre todo en Zaragoza, uno de mis referentes por posición. Fue jugador de trabajo también, con una carrera larga y un estilo de juego que me gusta. Tengo buena relación con él, yo fui su capitán en Zaragoza, creo que hicimos buenas migas y le guardo muy buen recuerdo. También me alegro muchísimo por él porque creo que se ha encontrado ante una oportunidad que, por supuesto, merecía. Aparte de haber sido un gran profesional como jugador, también tenía mucha madera de entrenador y yo creo que en ese sentido el Cholo no ha sido tonto y se lo ha llevado con él. P. ¿Tú qué tal aquí en Getafe? La sensación que nos dio a nosotros es que fue una operación exprés, ¿Cómo fue esa llegada? R. Fue todo muy rápido. Fue muy duro, obviamente, salir de Zaragoza porque yo he estado toda mi vida ligado al club. Es un club que siempre va a estar en mi corazón, soy zaragocista y siempre seré zaragocista. Es una realidad, eso no lo va a cambiar nadie. Me hubiese gustado salir de otra manera, que hubiese podido haber más tiempo, pero las circunstancias, sobre todo ya no del Zaragoza, sino del Getafe, demandaban eso. Había poca cantidad de jugadores, ya empezaba la competición europea, empezaba la Conference, había bajas en el equipo y tocó hacerlo todo súper rápido. Estoy agradecido porque me llegó la oportunidad de dar un cambio tan grande, de poder jugar en Europa, de poder debutar en Primera División y de poder cumplir un sueño. Estoy súper agradecido al Getafe y al míster, sobre todo, que es el que ha confiado en mí en ese sentido. Ahora estoy aquí para intentar devolver esa confianza, trabajar, disfrutar, aprender y crecer, no solo como persona, sino también como jugador, para, ojalá, poder dar muchos más saltos en mi carrera. Vengo también de una lesión y de una operación, y todavía estoy con un poquito de altibajos. Me operé en mayo, han pasado cinco meses. Todavía hay semanas en las que estoy mejor y semanas en las que estoy peor, pero poco a poco cada día estoy mejor. Ojalá también lo note en mi rendimiento para poder ayudar y aportar lo que yo aporto, que es trabajo y ser un jugador de equipo. El fútbol pone esas pequeñas trabas a sus mejores guerreros. P. Volviendo al fichaje, ¿cómo asimilas estar con Ibai haciendo una pretemporada para un equipo de Primera Federación y dos días después estar jugando contra el Partizán en Conference League? R. Yo siempre digo que lo más importante en la carrera del futbolista, en el deporte, es la cabeza. La cabeza es la herramienta más importante, la que te hace funcionar todo el cuerpo. Por el tiempo que llevaba en Zaragoza, por mi rol dentro del equipo y por todo lo que había sufrido y habíamos sufrido todos los zaragocistas, quizás me había preparado mucho mentalmente para que, cuando llegase el momento de dar ese salto y estar en un sitio de nivel deportivo, estuviese preparado. Creo que eso es lo que me ha hecho poder adaptarme rápido y bien, e intentar dar el rendimiento inmediato que se me demandaba. Sobre todo, a lo que voy es al tema de la mente, a estar preparado mentalmente. Muchas veces pasa: el tren pasa una vez en el fútbol, el fútbol va súper rápido y, como no lo cojas o no seas capaz de subirte, nunca sabes cuándo puede volver a pasar. Me llegó esta oportunidad y nunca sabes cuándo puede ser la última oportunidad de llegar al máximo nivel del fútbol español y mundial, porque yo creo que jugar en Primera División española es algo por lo que todo el mundo se cambiaría por mí. P. Por lo que me estás contando, aún no hemos visto al mejor Francho, ¿no? R. No soy mucho de hablar de mí ni de mi rendimiento, pero sé que físicamente llegará un día en el que mi rodilla asimile toda la carga. Es verdad que este es un cuerpo técnico que tiene una forma dura de trabajo, que me parece genial, porque si luego quieres demandar altos esfuerzos... P. Aquí se entrena duro, ¿eh? R. Por eso esto es como una pequeña dosis de lo que se está convirtiendo el fútbol. Se está convirtiendo en un deporte de contacto físico, de repetir esfuerzos y de jugadores dinámicos. Cada vez se ve menos el pie a pie, el tiqui-taca del Barcelona, que era un equipo que tenía el tiqui-taca súper dominado. Ahora mismo es el equipo que mejor presiona, que más arriba… P. ¿Qué tal precisamente con el míster? ¿Qué te va pidiendo ahora? ¿Es tan carismático como parece desde fuera? R. Es un poco lo que dice, ‘esto es fútbol, papá’. Es el papá de un poco de todos. Es el gestor. Más que un entrenador de fútbol, que por supuesto quién va a dudar de Bordalás como entrenador con lo que ha conseguido, es ese gestor que intenta siempre tenerte al 100 %. Te lleva al límite en muchos momentos, casi siempre, porque lo que quiere es que mejores. Te recomienda cosas, incluso en nuestra vida deportiva, para poder mejorar. Está siempre encima tuyo y creo que, en ese sentido, conmigo está siendo cariñoso, está muy encima mío. Creo que ambos nos tenemos mucho cariño. Yo a él siempre le estaré agradecido porque es la persona que ha confiado en mí para dar este salto en mi carrera. Es un poco ese padre, esa figura que todo el mundo... Ya solo con su presencia es respetable, es un tío que se hace respetar mucho y que ha conseguido algo a base de trabajo y, sobre todo, de ir jugador por jugador, sacando el mayor rendimiento y yendo a lo mental, que, como decía antes, creo que en el mundo del deporte es lo más importante. P. Como hombre de fútbol, cuando el Getafe no estaba ni en tus planes el año pasado, ¿qué piensas o qué percibes al ver al equipo meterse en Conference League? R. Para mí es admiración. Sobre todo, decir que si tantos años el Getafe se mantiene y ya ha habido un par de años que se ha metido en Europa, es porque algo están haciendo bien. Todos los años está ahí, es un equipo duro al que es difícil ganar. Muchos clubes se tienen que fijar también un poco en esa forma de trabajar. El Getafe, históricamente hablando, es un equipo más pequeño que muchos otros, pero ahora mismo, de hecho, el año pasado estuvo dentro del top ocho de la Primera División española, y eso no lo regala nadie. Es algo de admirar y que no se puede perder porque creo que ese ADN y esa identidad que el míster intenta implementar llevan muchos años dando resultado. Ojalá pueda prolongarlo muchos más años en el tiempo. P. Y ahora estando dentro, ¿qué opinas o qué sensación tienes, en lo personal y por lo que percibes del vestuario, de las críticas que recibe el Getafe por su juego? R. Y este año, de momento, no hemos empezado como queríamos y sabemos que tenemos que aplicarnos fuera de casa, que nos está costando mucho. Pero, si conseguimos sacar la situación adelante y hacer un buen año, no va a ser porque peguemos más patadas que nadie ni porque juguemos un fútbol más sucio que nadie. Cada equipo juega sus armas y, si nosotros somos fuertes y tenemos unas fortalezas, intentamos aprovecharlas al máximo y exponer lo menos posible nuestras debilidades. Es cuestión de fútbol y para eso está el cuerpo técnico y los propios jugadores, que nos conocemos entre nosotros para saber en qué somos buenos y en qué somos peores. Todos los equipos tienen sus cosas buenas y sus cosas malas. Hay que minimizar errores, minimizar debilidades y aprovechar nuestras máximas virtudes. El Getafe siempre ha sido un equipo que se basa en la seguridad defensiva, que es lo más importante. Si no encajas gol, mínimo tienes un punto. Es una realidad. Cuando tienes un punto siempre va a ser más fácil poder tener alguno más. Dicho esto, este año tenemos que dar una vuelta a eso porque nos está costando mucho más mantener la portería a cero. Es algo en lo que el míster insiste mucho y tiene toda la razón. Tenemos que darle una vuelta y seguir apretándonos los machos para volver un poco a lo que era el Getafe. P. ¿Qué le pasa al equipo defensivamente en los balones parados? R. No sé si decía el cuerpo técnico que somos el equipo al que más le rematan. Es un dato que ahora mismo en el fútbol no se puede permitir, y menos un club como nosotros, que nos basamos en la seguridad defensiva y damos mucha importancia al balón parado. Es un debe muy grande que tenemos que corregir ya, porque el tiempo pasa y, si no pones remedio a tiempo, luego vienen las lamentaciones y ya no hay margen de cambiar las cosas. P. Te pregunto por tus compañeros en el medio del campo, los Mangala, Terrats y compañía. ¿Qué tal con ellos? R. Muy bien. Además, yo me considero una persona que me llevo bien con todo el mundo, me adapto a cualquier perfil y a cualquier personalidad. Siempre pienso que cada uno es como es y cada uno tiene su forma de ser. Son jugadores de nivel top y yo soy un privilegiado por poderme juntar en el campo con ellos. Aprendo mucho y espero que ellos también puedan aprender de mí. Estoy súper feliz, no solo con los mediocentros, sino con todo el club en general. Es un club pequeño, humilde, muy familiar, en el que te conoces todos con todos y todos son buena gente. No es casualidad que todo el Getafe lleve tanto tiempo a tan buen nivel. Es cuestión de trabajar desde una base y que todos remen en la misma dirección, y eso se nota. P. Te pregunto por tu Real Zaragoza. Al menos en este caso, desde fuera, puedes estar contento de que el equipo está yendo bastante bien. R. Sí, yo eso siempre lo he dicho. Me alegraré siempre por todo lo bueno que les pase. Ojalá consigan lo que todos merecen, tanto jugadores como directiva y, sobre todo, la afición, que lleva tantos años tragando. Se trata de conseguirlo otra vez, volver al fútbol profesional, a Segunda División. Creo que se están haciendo las cosas bien y que, más pronto que tarde, volverá a donde se merece. Yo, por supuesto, me alegraré mucho porque lo siento como una parte de mí y siempre estaré con ellos. P. Ahora la cosa parece que va bien… R. Sí. Sobre todo, es que están siendo muy regulares, y eso es lo más importante en todas las categorías del fútbol, pero más en una Primera RFEF. Creo que están haciendo las cosas bien y trabajando muy bien. Si siguen así, no digo que lo consigan seguro porque nunca sabes lo que va a pasar, pero estarán muy cerca de conseguir el objetivo. P. Al final es duro para un equipo histórico verse en esta situación, ¿verdad? R. Mira, yo jugué allí también, soy de Zaragoza y es duro porque es complicado. Nadie lo merece, sobre todo la gente que ha vivido muchos momentos del Zaragoza y no merece vivir eso. Pero, por desgracia, ha tocado y creo que lo están afrontando bien. Seguro que vuelven a donde merecen, que es, como mínimo, Segunda División, y por supuesto a Primera dentro de poco.

articles.title: Misery Index: Big Ten's reign at the top of college football might be over after rash of QB injuries
articles.summary: After a string of bad luck, it's possible the Big Ten only gets one team into the College Football Playoff this season.
articles.body:
In college football, bragging rights are almost worth as much as trophies. Yes, after an eight-year drought (which was preceded by an 11-year drought), winning three straight national championships was a huge deal for the Big Ten. But while the hunk of metal that Michigan (2023), Ohio State (2024) and Indiana (2025) got to take home is nice to look at, the element that's unique to college football is being able to tell the SEC "We're better than you" and having a scoreboard back it up.

At least at the top of the league, the Big Ten was better than the SEC for three straight seasons. Winning the College Football Playoff with three different programs, while the SEC wasn't even represented in the championship game, made it inarguable.

It was fresh and exciting for a league that couldn't hold a candle to the SEC's success in the modern era.

But now, thanks to a crazy run of quarterback injuries, it's over.

Yes, the Big Ten will have a representative in this year's CFP. But after UCLA's expensive loss to Michigan and Indiana's puzzling performance at Washington , there's now a scenario where the Big Ten is a one-bid league and doesn't even come within sniffing distance of the championship game.

As we sit here after the penultimate week of the regular season, it's fair to say the Big Ten's four best teams this season were Oregon, Ohio State, Indiana and UCLA. All four will end the season with major quarterback problems that almost certainly will crush their chances of a deep run.

On Sept. 26, Oregon's Heisman contender Dante Moore suffered a concussion after a dirty hit by USC's Desman Stephens and hasn't played since. Oregon went into a nosedive and fired the offensive coordinator but has played better since. At 8-3 and ranked No. 13, however, the Ducks have a very narrow path to a playoff bid.

Near the end of Ohio State's 19-15 win at Indiana on Oct. 17, Julian Sayin took an awkward hit that caused a significant arm injury . Freshman Luke Fahey wasn't ready to take his place, but the Buckeyes' problems are deeper than one player. They've spiraled on both sides of the ball and are completely out of the mix now at 7-4 after a 31-28 loss at Nebraska .

Indiana's Josh Hoover has been banged up for much of the season, and at times backup Grant Wilson has looked more effective. But in Indiana's 27-24 loss at Washington, Curt Cignetti played both and didn't get great results from either. At 9-2, Indiana's problem is that USC remains its best win. The committee will likely punish them for that in next week's rankings.

And now UCLA, which has been the darling of the sport this year, might be down to its third quarterback after Ty Dieffenbach was carted off late in an 18-16 triple-overtime loss to Michigan. If UCLA loses to USC next week to finish 10-2, its playoff prospects could be very much in doubt.

It's getting so desperate in the Big Ten that the league's best shot to win a fourth straight national title might be … Iowa? And the Hawkeyes, ranked No. 15 this week, would probably need to win the Big Ten to get in — which would require the perfect combination of results next week just for them to qualify for that championship game.

This is mostly just a string of bad luck for the Big Ten. But it's also a trend we should probably get used to now that these teams will have to play 10 power conference games to qualify for the 24-team playoff beginning next year.

Because of how talent has been spread around in the NIL era, teams are struggling with depth more than they ever have while also playing a more physically demanding schedule. That combination leads to a cascade of injuries. For instance, if you have a decimated offensive line, your quarterback and running backs are going to be more at risk. It's all connected, and winning a national title will be surviving a war of attrition.

The Big Ten, it seems, is poised to lose that war as the 2026 season winds down. Whether it's Oregon and Ohio State getting knocked off the national title path or UCLA struggling to hang onto its once-in-a-lifetime dream season, the Big Ten's reign is coming to a luckless end.

It's rare that the Misery Index honors an entire conference rather than one team, but the circumstances of this season have been so spectacularly fluky and frustrating that America's most miserable fan base for Week 12 is anyone associated with the Big Ten conference.

ACC: The future of Bill Belichick will be a fascinating topic as the season winds down. At one point, it truly looked like the Tar Heels were turning the corner, playing a better brand of football and showing proof of concept for what Belichick-style football could be at the college level. But what does it all amount to at the end? After a 41-24 loss at Virginia, North Carolina is 9-14 under Belichick overall and needs to beat NC State next week to become bowl eligible. The Tar Heels will probably get that done and be able to claim some progress, but the 74-year-old Belichick was not hired to build slowly. Even under the best of circumstances, you've got a short window with the most successful NFL coach of all time, and every year that passes without a major breakthrough will naturally lead to questions about whether North Carolina should just start all over again. If you're in the mood for generosity, the Tar Heels lost to Louisville by two, to Miami by three, to Syracuse by one in overtime and to Clemson by eight. If they just make a couple more plays in two of those games, everything looks different. But when you zoom out and ask if the Belichick gambit was worth its time, North Carolina can't argue it's paid off at all yet. Whether Belichick should back for Year 3 is an interesting question. If North Carolina feels close enough to give it one last try, Belichick should get that opportunity. But if this mediocrity is what it's going to be like in 2027, why waste everyone's time?

Big 12: Maybe the only consistent theme of the Deion Sanders era at Colorado is how often the head coach comes into the press room after losses and talks about how his team is so much better than what it says on the scoreboard. "This is a good, solid football team," Sanders said after a 35-28 loss at Cincinnati. "I know the record is not indicative of that, and it's disappointing and I don't even understand … it don't seem like to me the better team was victorious, but they were because they did what they needed to do." Enough of this — not just the refusal to acknowledge reality but the entire Sanders era. He's had four years. At 4-7, Colorado is guaranteed to finish with a losing record in three of them. Colorado has lost 10 straight on the road in conference play. If this were anyone but Coach Prime, we would already be speculating about who would replace him. But Sanders has generated so much attention and money for Colorado athletics that it will be difficult to cut the cord — particularly with a buyout in the $25 million range. It's a shame for college football that Sanders has become kind of your garden-variety Big 12 coach because the 2024 season was truly electric. But without Shedeur Sanders at quarterback and Travis Hunter doing everything on both sides of the ball, it's a pretty underwhelming and uninteresting product. The entire point of Deion Sanders was to be different, but a lot of coaches could lose seven or eight games a year at Colorado.

SEC: Though not surprising given the way LSU's season has gone, it is absolutely stunning in the big picture to look at the SEC standings and see the Tigers much closer to the bottom of the league than the top. College football is crazy right now, with most teams having a collection of good wins and bad losses that make it hard to pinpoint exactly what they are. LSU, however, has made it simple in Lane Kiffin's first year. They're the definition of mediocre. LSU has beaten Clemson, Louisiana Tech, Texas A&M, McNeese State, Mississippi State and Auburn — all opponents they can out-talent. They have lost to Ole Miss, Kentucky, Alabama, Texas and Tennessee — all opponents that have similar talent. Even though some of those games could have easily gone the other direction (not Saturday's 27-13 loss to Tennessee, which was fairly comprehensive), that particular trend has to be concerning to LSU fans. If Kiffin needs to have a clear talent advantage to contend for titles, it's not going to happen in the SEC regardless of how much money LSU is willing to spend on his roster. When you play this many quality opponents, you have to out-coach somebody at some point. For LSU to go an entire season and not pull out a single game where it was a coin flip at the beginning? That's a major indictment of Kiffin's first season in Baton Rouge.

Group of Six: South Florida thought it had wrapped up its coaching search a year ago with Texas A&M offensive coordinator Collin Klein. Then it became clear the Kansas State job was going to open (it's Klein's alma mater) and USF was forced to scramble at the last minute. It landed on Brian Hartline, who had been Ohio State's wide receivers coach since 2018 and had recruited a bunch of players out of Florida. So the hire made sense on paper, particularly after he called plays last year for the first time in his career. But in the real world, after seeing Hartline's first 11 games at South Florida, the school will need to think seriously about whether to give him a second season. That might be a harsh judgment on someone who is dealing with the learning curve of becoming a head coach. But this is arguably the best job in the American Conference given the geography and possibly the biggest roster budget in the league. Despite one of the most favorable schedules in college football, South Florida being 6-5 after a 35-14 thumping at Florida Atlantic is completely unacceptable, and the USF administration should look at itself in the mirror and ask itself if it did enough due diligence on Hartline to understand his strengths and weaknesses from the Ohio State perspective. Hint: It didn't.

Ryan Day: We are all going to have to get used to elite coaches having bad seasons in this volatile era, but it hits harder at a place like Ohio State that almost never experiences a true disaster. In fact, the last time the Buckeyes flopped like this was going 6-7 in 2011 amidst the chaos of Jim Tressel's ouster. (Then Urban Meyer came in and went 12-0 the following season.) Because Ohio State gets the most intense media coverage of any program in the country, this entire offseason will center around a grim autopsy of what went wrong. Most likely, the conversation will center on Day's decision to go NFL-heavy with his recent coordinator hires. Bringing in Matt Patricia to run the defense and Arthur Smith to be offensive coordinator may be fine decisions individually, but it does not feel like they have left Ohio State in a better spot than they were in with Chip Kelly and Jim Knowles in the coordinator suite. We'll see how Day responds, but he will surely do something because he's poised to start 2027 back in the same tenuous spot he was before winning the national title.

Matt Campbell: Of the many things that will rankle Penn State fans about this nightmare season, which stands at 6-5 with a game at Maryland left to finish up, let's focus on Campbell's hat. There's a sweet story behind why Campbell wears a worn-out cap with a deeply-bent brim on the sideline. It's a tribute to his grandfather, who worked two jobs and worked the graveyard shift at a Ford plant. It reminds Campbell of his blue-collar roots, so ever since he became a head coach at Toledo, he has worn one hat all season long, no matter how gross or faded it gets. Here's the problem, though. It's great to have a blue-collar mentality, but this is the big leagues of college football. Working hard isn't enough. If you're trying to win the way Penn State demands of its coaches, you need more five-star talent than five-star want-to. Does Campbell understand that? He should, especially now after a 25-24 loss at home to Rutgers that marks the absolute rock bottom for Campbell's first year. If your team isn't working hard enough to beat Rutgers (or Northwestern or Wisconsin), the blue-collar image you're trying to represent looks like fake hustle. And if your team isn't talented enough to win those games, then you've got the wrong person leading the program. We have to tell the truth. As annoying as James Franklin had become to Penn State's administration and fan base, particularly after a losing streak last season that sealed his fate, everything the school has done subsequently has made the decision to fire him look like a mistake.

Charles Huff: Memphis' coach has been a popular name in the Maryland coaching search, and Huff isn't doing much to knock down the speculation. At a recent press conference, in fact, Huff offered an eyebrow-raising quote about his future, saying he isn't worried about the chatter from a recruiting standpoint because "if I'm leaving Memphis, I ain't going to high school, I'm going to something bigger." Well, this weekend, Huff had an opportunity to make a good impression in the state of Maryland and let a massive opportunity slide by in a 38-34 loss at Navy. Memphis led this game 34-24 and had the ball before punting with about eight minutes left. Everything that happened after that point was a disaster, with Navy scoring on a 68-yard touchdown run, Memphis going three-and-out on the ensuing possession and the Midshipmen scoring the winning touchdown with 15 seconds left. This is a particularly egregious loss for Memphis because the Tigers haven't won the American Conference title since 2019 and beating Navy would have almost assured them of a spot in the championship game. They still have a good shot of making it via tiebreakers, but beating Navy would have kept Memphis alive for the CFP if Boise State stumbled somewhere. That's definitely off the table now.

Manny Diaz: Maybe it's a good thing that Diaz pulled out of the Florida State search earlier this week because Seminole fans would not have been happy campers if he was still in the mix coming off a terrible 20-10 home loss to Clemson. Yes, it says a lot about the job Diaz has done at Duke that losing to Clemson is now an upset. But, indeed, the Blue Devils were more than 10-point favorites facing a Clemson team down to its third-string quarterback. That was a juicy opportunity for Duke to get its eighth win and for the fan base to pound its chest because the Duke coach wasn't interested in leaving for Florida State. Instead, Clemson had the better game plan by devoting all its resources to stopping star running back Nate Sheppard (19 carries, 116 yards) and forcing Duke to make some plays in the passing game. The Blue Devils couldn't do it, struggled to adjust and gained just 247 total yards. Duke will never complain about bowl eligibility given the program's history, but the whole point of Diaz sticking around for the long haul is to raise the floor and the expectations to a level where losing games like this is disappointing.

A Ramblin' Wreck of love: Things got so out of hand in Georgia Tech's 50-29 loss to Wake Forest that the ESPN broadcast turned away from the action on the field and focused on what appeared to be a young couple's argument in the stands , with former Florida quarterback Jesse Palmer doing a play-by-play of the interaction. We sincerely feel for that couple, who surely did not attend to a college football game intending to become a viral internet meme. But when a game goes off the rails and announcers need to fill dead air, stuff happens. At least by the time the broadcast circled back, the couple was kissing and seemed to have made up. But that may be the last bit of love this season for Georgia Tech fans, who have watched their program spiral to 3-8, fire a bunch of assistant coaches and lose their last three home games by a combined 70 points. Head coach Brent Key will be under a lot of pressure to fix what broke this fall — not counting this couple's relationship issues.

Curtains for Curtis: This week could have been the big breakout for Vanderbilt freshman quarterback Jared Curtis, the Nashville native who switched his commitment from Georgia to his hometown school with a big NIL deal attached. Curtis had gotten the Commodores to within 27-24 at Florida and was driving inside the 25-yard line with a chance to take the lead and around seven minutes on the clock. Instead, Curtis took an awkward hit on second down, aggravating a wrist injury he's been dealing with and fumbling the ball. Though Vanderbilt retained possession, it was a tough spot to insert backup Whit Muschamp (yes, the son of Texas defensive coordinator Will Muschamp), who watched his first snap hit him in the chest for a 12-yard loss. Though Vandy tied the game on a 51-yard field goal, Florida scored on the next possession and won 34-27. We'll never know what could have happened if Curtis stayed in the game and gave Vanderbilt the lead.

Border-town blues: UTEP fired another coach this week, letting 37-year-old Scotty Walden go after winning just six of his 34 games. Nobody will blame the school for looking at the results and deciding it needs to spin the coaching roulette wheel once again. But is this the most difficult job in FBS? A 52-3 loss to Air Force in the first game post-Walden serves as a reminder of just how hard it's going to be for anyone to get this program going. Since 2000, UTEP has had five coaches. Dana Dimel went to one bowl game in six years. Sean Kugler went to one in five years. Mike Price managed to get bowl eligible three times in nine years. Gary Nord went 8-4 in his first season and then 6-30 over the next three. Look, any program can strike gold with a coach or a star quarterback and turn things around. New Mexico hasn't been a ton better historically than UTEP and is now on the precipice of winning the Mountain West. But between the program's awful track record, its isolated geography and inability to spend its way to relevance, UTEP needs a lot of luck with its next hire.
