articles.title: B/R's 2026 College Football Experts Top 25 Rankings After Week 12
articles.summary: The Big Ten was dealt a crushing blow on Saturday as UCLA, Indiana and Ohio State all suffered upset losses, shaking up the conference standings and the College Football Playoff picture.
articles.body:
The Big Ten was dealt a crushing blow on Saturday as UCLA, Indiana and Ohio State all suffered upset losses, shaking up the conference standings and the College Football Playoff picture.

The Bruins and Hoosiers both lost in overtime, while BYU needed its own overtime victory to avoid joining the list of Week 12 upsets.

With plenty of shuffling at the bottom of the Top 25 picture, the four-loss SEC teams have entered the conversation, including an Oklahoma team that had been relegated to an afterthought after a disappointing start.

Ahead is an updated look at how the college football experts here at B/R line up the nation's top 25 teams following Week 12 action.

Week 12 Result: WIN vs UTEP (52-3) Next Week: at New Mexico

The Falcons lead the nation with 351.7 rushing yards per game, and they blew past that total on Friday night with 429 yards on 64 carries in a blowout victory over a 10-loss UTEP squad. With nearly double the time of possession on offense and two takeaways on defense, Air Force dominated across the board, and the Falcons have now matched their win total from the last two seasons combined. They face Mountain West leader New Mexico on the road in the regular-season finale next Friday.

Week 12 Result: WIN vs. Samford (59-17) Next Week: at Alabama

The Tigers sprinted out to a 52-3 halftime lead and racked up 672 total yards en route to an easy victory over an FCS opponent, priming the pump for the Iron Bowl next weekend. Backup quarterback Tristan Ti'a completed 17-of-18 pass attempts for 341 yards and five total touchdowns, while Jeremiah Cobb (10 carries, 120 yards, 1 TD) led a running game that averaged 6.4 yards per carry in a dominant win.

Week 12 Result: WIN at Wyoming (24-17) Next Week: vs. Air Force

A fumble and a missed field goal in the fourth quarter opened the door for 10 unanswered points from Wyoming, but New Mexico managed to hang on to remain atop the Mountain West standings with a 6-1 record in conference play. The Lobos have one of the best run defenses in the country, allowing just 73.5 yards per game, and the Cowboys clocked in well below that with 46 yards and 1.8 yards per carry on the night.

Week 12 Result: WIN vs. Texas A&M (28-7) Next Week: at Missouri

John Mateer had 269 passing yards, 66 rushing yards and four touchdowns, with three of those scores coming in a decisive 21-point fourth quarter. The Sooners have quietly won three straight after victories over Florida and Ole Miss the last two games, and have rallied to a 5-3 record in SEC play after a disappointing start to the year.

21. Boise State (9-2, Previous Rank: 13)

Week 12 Result: LOSS vs. San Diego State (20-22) Next Week: TBD (flex game)

A puzzling decision to go for it on fourth down led to a turnover on downs, setting up the game-winning 42-yard field goal for San Diego State kicker Cooper DiLeva as time expired. With that, the Broncos' hopes of earning the Group of Six playoff bid were dealt a major blow, potentially knocking them behind Liberty in the rankings.

Week 12 Result: WIN vs. Vanderbilt (34-27) Next Week: at Florida State

The Gators improved to 5-4 in SEC play by squeezing out a victory over Vanderbilt, with Jadan Baugh (19 carries, 76 yards, 1 TD) scoring the go-ahead touchdown with 2:18 remaining and the Gators defense forcing a turnover on downs on Vanderbilt's ensuing possession. Aaron Philo finished with 241 passing yards, 73 rushing yards and two rushing touchdowns. With Florida State to close out the regular season next weekend, the Gators have clinched their first winning record in conference play since 2020.

Week 12 Result: WIN vs. Western Kentucky (45-14) Next Week: at Missouri State

The Flames found the end zone on each of their first four offensive possessions to build a 28-0 lead, then coasted to victory for their second 10-win season in four years under head coach Jamey Chadwell, turning things around after a 4-8 finish in 2025. Deshawn Purdie finished with 344 passing yards and two touchdowns, while Liberty outrushed Western Kentucky by a 216-54 margin and found the end zone four more times on the ground. Will they overtake Boise State in the CFB rankings?

Week 12 Result: WIN vs. Pittsburgh (42-10) Next Week: at Kentucky

Lincoln Kienholz had never thrown more than two passing touchdowns in a game prior to Saturday, but torched the Pitt secondary for 309 yards and five touchdowns in a blowout victory. Tre Richardson (8 catches, 114 yards, 2 TD) and Lawayne McCoy (5 catches, 63 yards, 2 TD) led the way in the receiving game, and the defense did its part with four takeaways and only 150 total yards allowed. Now Louisville will look to make it three straight wins against in-state rival Kentucky next weekend to close out the regular season.

Week 12 Result: WIN at West Virginia (34-31) Next Week: vs. Baylor

True freshman Keisean Henderson threw for 268 yards and a touchdown starting in place of the injured Conner Weigman. He led a 13-play, 87-yard drive to tie the game early in the fourth quarter and an eight-play, 34-yard drive to set up the game-winning 23-yard field goal from Jonathan Dimas. The Cougars leaned heavily on the running game, with Makhi Hughes (19 carries, 158 yards, 3 TD) leading the charge. The defense also did a solid job keeping electric dual-threat quarterback Michael Hawkins Jr. in check as he finished with 228 total yards and two touchdowns.

Week 12 Result: WIN at Kansas State (35-28, OT) Next Week: vs. Arizona State

Noah Fifita threw for 323 yards and two touchdowns with a third score on the ground, and the Wildcats were able to grind out a victory in rainy conditions. Giovanni Richardson had a 25-yard touchdown reception on the second play of overtime, and the Arizona defense held up in the red zone with a stop on fourth and one to clinch the victory.

Week 12 Result: WIN vs. Maryland (35-21) Next Week: at UCLA

Jayden Maiava went over 3,000 yards passing on the season with a 237-yard, two-touchdown performance, with the bulk of the damage going to freshman Trent Mosley, who had eight catches for 78 yards and both scores. On a day when UCLA, Indiana and Ohio State all lost, the Trojans improved their standing heading into next weekend's annual showdown with UCLA.

Week 12 Result: WIN at Michigan State (45-7) Next Week: vs. Washington

Dylan Raiola threw for 234 yards and a touchdown, but it was the Oregon running game that led the charge in Friday night's victory over Michigan State. The Ducks' rushing attack logged 188 yards and five scores, with Brandon Smith (14 carries, 121 yards, 2 TD) leading the way as they averaged 4.9 yards per carry. The defense also had two takeaways and surrendered just 200 yards of total offense, as the Ducks have now won four in a row.

Week 12 Result: LOSS at Washington (24-27, OT) Next Week: vs. Purdue

The Hoosiers scored two first quarter touchdowns, then saw their offense stall, ultimately going back to benched starter Josh Hoover at quarterback to try to jumpstart things. The bigger surprise was the Indiana defense surrendering a season-high 443 total yards, including the game-tying, 74-yard touchdown drive with 3:34 remaining. A missed 37-yard field goal from Paddy McAteer would have sent the game to a second overtime, but instead wrapped up Indiana's second loss of the year.

Week 12 Result: WIN at Illinois (34-17) Next Week: vs. Nebraska

The Iowa defense had two takeaways and a touchdown as the Hawkeyes improved to 9-2 and kept their College Football Playoff hopes alive. L.J. Phillips (26 carries, 154 yards, 1 TD) anchored the rushing attack, and Iowa outgained Illinois by a lopsided 263-28 margin on the ground. A win over Nebraska next weekend is a must if their playoff hopes are going to survive, though they would need a lot to break right to make the Big Ten championship game.

Week 12 Result: WIN at Kansas (31-29, 3 OT) Next Week: vs. Cincinnati

BYU nearly picked up what would have been a catastrophic third loss by allowing 10 unanswered points to Kansas in the fourth quarter, forcing overtime. The two sides traded blows through two overtime periods before the Cougars converted their two-point conversion in the third overtime to avoid the upset. Bear Bachmeier had 173 passing yards, 59 rushing yards and two rushing touchdowns, while LJ Martin tallied 25 carries for 127 yards and a score.

Latest Bowl Predictions, 2026 College Football Playoff Picks amid Bracket Scenarios

Week 12 Result: LOSS at Michigan (16-18, 3OT) Next Week: vs. USC

An injury to Ty Dieffenbach on the first play of overtime forced third-string signal caller Madden Iamaleava into action with an undefeated season on the line, and the Bruins settled for kicking a pair of field goals before failing to convert their two-point attempt in the third overtime. Zooming out from the injury, the UCLA rushing attack was held to 107 yards and 2.5 yards per carry after entering the game averaging 202.7 yards per game, so credit where it's due to the Michigan defense.

Week 12 Result: WIN at Baylor (20-10) Next Week: vs. TCU

The Red Raiders overcame three turnovers to improve to 7-1 in Big 12 play and reach 10 wins for the second year in a row. J'Koby Williams (21 carries, 117 yards, 1 TD) and Thomas Castellanos (18 carries, 92 yards) anchored a Texas Tech running game that finished with a 231-31 edge in rushing yardage, and the defense allowed 1.4 yards per carry and 4.9 yards per pass attempt. A win over TCU next weekend would punch the Red Raiders' ticket to the Big 12 championship game.

8. Wake Forest (10-1, Previous Rank: 10)

Week 12 Result: WIN at Georgia Tech (50-29) Next Week: vs. Duke

Gio Lopez and the high-powered Wake Forest offense were too much for Georgia Tech, as the Demon Deacons piled up 607 total yards en route to an eighth straight victory and just the third 10-win season in program history. Lopez finished with 324 passing yards and two touchdowns while logging two more scores on the ground, and he is quietly emerging on the periphery of the Heisman Trophy race with 33 total touchdowns on the year.

Week 12 Result: WIN vs. Chattanooga (47-0) Next Week: vs. Auburn

Austin Mack threw for 254 yards and had five total touchdowns in his first collegiate start as the Crimson Tide took advantage of the opportunity against an FCS opponent and rested Keelon Russell, who has been battling an ankle injury. The Alabama defense allowed just 86 total yards and five first downs in the shutout, dominating an overmatched opponent in what amounted to a tune-up before the Iron Bowl next weekend.

Week 12 Result: WIN vs. LSU (27-13) Next Week: at Vanderbilt

The Volunteers pounded out an 11-play, 63-yard touchdown drive early in the fourth quarter to take a 20-13 lead, then forced a fumble on LSU's ensuing offensive possession before Faizon Brandon sealed the win with a 55-yard rushing score. Both teams turned the ball over three times, and the difference was the Tennessee defense shutting down LSU's running game, allowing 43 yards on 34 carries and forcing three fumbles. The Volunteers continue to find enough offense to support their standout defense, even if the stats don't jump off the page.

5. Texas Longhorns (9-2, Previous Rank: 7)

Week 12 Result: WIN vs. Arkansas (45-3) Next Week: at Texas A&M

Arch Manning was an efficient 21-of-25 passing for 287 yards and two touchdowns, and he also added a rushing score to lead the onslaught in a lopsided victory over Arkansas.

The Razorbacks were fresh off an upset win against South Carolina last weekend, but the Longhorns defense had two interceptions and forced four turnovers on downs and two punts while keeping them out of the end zone.

Texas still has a path to the SEC championship game, but should be a College Football Playoff lock as long as they beat Texas A&M next weekend.

4. Miami Hurricanes (10-1, Previous Rank: 5)

Week 12 Result: WIN vs. Virginia Tech (28-20) Next Week: vs. Boston College

The Hurricanes came back from down 14-0 to clinch a spot in the ACC championship game, where they will face off against Wake Forest for the second time this year after beating the Demon Deacons by a 33-20 score back on Sept. 18.

Darian Mensah threw two interceptions and didn't have a touchdown pass for the first time this season, but Mark Fletcher Jr. (16 carries, 63 yards, 3 TD) picked up the slack offensively, and the Hurricanes defense did the rest.

The Hokies managed just 208 total yards, and they were held to just a single field goal after halftime to open the door for the Miami comeback.

3. Notre Dame Fighting Irish (10-1, Previous Rank: 4)

Week 12 Result: WIN vs. SMU (24-3) Next Week: at Syracuse

An SMU offense that entered the game averaging 34.0 points per game was limited to a single field goal in a smothering performance by the Notre Dame defense to give the Fighting Irish a quality win against a previously ranked opponent.

CJ Carr had 312 passing yards and a touchdown, Nolan James Jr. tallied 98 rushing yards and two touchdowns and the Notre Dame defense forced four punts and three turnovers on downs while also coming away with an interception.

Assuming they take care of business on the road against Syracuse next weekend, the Fighting Irish have punched their ticket to the College Football Playoff.

Week 12 Result: WIN at TCU (38-17) Next Week: vs. West Virginia

It looked like the Utes were in serious trouble when TCU scored 17 unanswered points to begin the second half to make it a 17-17 game, but more late-game heroics from Devon Dampier led Utah to victory.

Utah put together three fourth quarter touchdown drives, including a pass and a run from Dampier, who finished with 278 passing yards, 62 rushing yards and four total touchdowns.

West Virginia is the final obstacle standing between Utah and an undefeated regular season, setting up a battle between two of the nation's top dual-threat quarterbacks as Michael Hawkins Jr. comes to town.

1. Georgia Bulldogs (10-1, Previous Rank: 1)

Week 12 Result: WIN at South Carolina (34-6) Next Week: vs. Georgia Tech

The Bulldogs defense bottled up LaNorris Sellers, limiting South Carolina's standout quarterback to 87 passing yards, 24 rushing yards and an interception and blanking the Gamecocks in the second half after leading just 10-6 at halftime.

Gunner Stockton was an efficient 19-of-23 passing for 281 yards and a touchdown, while Nate Frazier anchored the rushing attack with 23 carries for 94 yards and two scores, providing more than enough offensive firepower in support of the defense.

Now the Bulldogs will wait and see who they play in the SEC championship game after finishing 8-1 in conference play, and they close out the regular season with a non-conference matchup against in-state rival Georgia Tech.

articles.title: Wales v Norway: Rhian Wilkinson rules out Jess Fishlock return for Women's World Cup play-off final
articles.summary: Rhian Wilkinson has not considered asking Jess Fishlock to come out of retirement for the Women's World Cup play-off final against Norway.
articles.body:
Rhian Wilkinson says she has not considered asking Jess Fishlock to come out of retirement even though the Wales legend will be on camp for the Women's World Cup play-off final against Norway.

Fishlock ended her playing career earlier this month after her Seattle Reign side lost to Gotham FC in the National Women's Soccer League (NWSL) play-offs.

The 39-year-old played on for one final season at Reign having retired from international football in October 2025.

Fishlock will be part of Wales' coaching staff for for next month's two-legged tie against the Norwegians, who visit the Cardiff City Stadium on Tuesday, 1 December, before the return leg in Oslo four days later.

Despite some speculation over whether Fishlock could play some part on the pitch, Wilkinson said: "I think you get retirement right when you know there's still something in you to give."

Women's World Cup qualifying play-off final first leg

Live on BBC iPlayer, BBC One Wales, BBC Sounds, BBC Radio Wales, Radio Cymru, BBC Sport website and app, plus live text commentary.

The Wales boss added: "It takes years to recognise that you got it right, because you're sort of [thinking] 'oh should I have kept playing', but when you get it wrong injuries and someone else makes the decision that you're finished, that's a tough way to to end your career.

"I think Jess has qualified [for Euro 2025], made history with Wales, done such a great job as well as building the game over in the US and equally so much in Wales.

"[But] she's retired. Jess is here to further her technical and tactical awareness, but also for her experiences and that kind of confidence that she brings to the environment."

While there will be no Fishlock, Wales will welcome back a number of experienced players from injury for the Norway games.

Wales are hoping to cause an upset as they bid to reach the Women's World Cup for the first time, though beating former champions Norway will likely not be enough to guarantee a place in Brazil next summer.

The complex nature of the qualification process means that Wales may have to negotiate inter-confederation play-offs next February to secure a World Cup place, even if they triumph over Norway.

articles.title: Yahoo Top 10: Wild Week 12 shakes up college football rankings
articles.summary: Utah, Georgia and Notre Dame all delivered on a chaotic Saturday of action, but the Big Ten's contenders suffered losses that will change the College Footbal...
articles.body:
The most mundane weekends in college football can often turn into mayhem.

Two of the Big Ten's best playoff challengers (UCLA and Indiana) lost, preseason No. 1 Ohio State took a fourth 'L' this season and LSU — its high-priced head coach, Lane Kiffin, and $40 million-plus roster — dropped a fifth game.

The Bruins and Hoosiers served up the biggest surprises with overtime losses at Michigan and Washington, respectively, tossing the conference into a bit of chaos and uncertainty. Can the Big Ten win a fourth straight national championship ? At this point, the odds seem steep for even getting more than two teams into the playoff. Also in the conference, Ohio State became the first preseason top-ranked team to lose at least four games since USC in 2012 as the Buckeyes dropped a game at Nebraska.

In the SEC, Tennessee kept its playoff hopes alive with a throttling of LSU in Knoxville, and Georgia survived the always-scary trip to Columbia, South Carolina. The Big 12 race is Utah, BYU and Texas Tech. Meanwhile, Miami and Wake Forest are on a collision course for a rematch in Charlotte (the Hurricanes won Round 1, 33-20) for all the ACC marbles.

The Utes blew open a 17-17 tie with three consecutive touchdowns in the final six minutes of the game. QB Devon Dampier scored the last two TDs — one passing and another rushing — on a night when he led the team on the ground and through the air. Dampier had more than 325 total yards and Larry Simmons caught three passes for a whopping 114 yards as Utah clinched a Big 12 championship game appearance.

Is anyone playing better football than Kirby Smart's crew? Smart's team turned a tight game into a blowout in the second half, even recovering a surprise onside kick in the third quarter. Gunner Stockton continues to be one of the nation's leaders in efficiency (19 of 23) and the Bulldogs know how to run the ball (Nate Frazier had 94 yards). But DC Glenn Schumann's defensive unit was great from the start in Columbia on Saturday night.

After beating Miami and bludgeoning SMU, there is little argument that the Irish, with a season-ending win over Syracuse next week, will make the 12-team postseason. The loss to BYU stings, sure, but Notre Dame QB CJ Carr continues to be one of the biggest challengers in the Heisman Trophy race. He threw for more than 300 yards against the Mustangs.

Down 14-0? No problem. The Hurricanes mounted a comeback at Hard Rock Stadium to solidify a trip to Charlotte for the ACC championship game — despite QB Darian Mensah not throwing a single touchdown pass. In fact, he had two interceptions to match his season total to this point. But Miami's defense rose to the challenge after the early hole, forcing Tech into five punts on its next seven drives.

If there was still any doubt that the Demon Deacons are real playoff challengers, those should be put to bed. Jake Dickert's team has outscored its last seven opponents 363-67. QB Gio Lopez threw for two touchdowns and ran for two more in the shellacking of the Yellow Jackets. Wake is barreling toward an ACC championship game appearance and a playoff spot.

The Tide rested Keelon Russell, and why not? The 7-5 FCS Mocs didn't stand a chance. Seven of Chattanooga's 10 drives lasted three plays or less. Kane Wommack, a candidate for several head coaching gigs, and his defensive unit has allowed 20 points the last three games. Bama is headed to the playoff with a win in the Iron Bowl.

Michigan QB Bryce Underwood completed just 11 passes and was sacked four times. And while that doesn't sound like the stat line of a winner, the Bruins offense couldn't muster enough to beat the Wolverines. Ty Dieffenbach was sacked four times, threw an interception and lost a costly fumble that set up Michigan for the go-ahead score.

Arch Manning had four incompletions and three touchdowns in the win over the lowly Razorbacks. There's no hiding the Longhorns' deficiencies, but Texas has the talent to win it all and a victory over the Aggies next week will send them to the 12-team playoff. After back-to-back losses to Florida and Oklahoma, the Horns have won five straight.

No one benefitted from Saturday's Big Ten upset bonanza quite like the Hawkeyes. They are now in striking distance to advance to the playoff. And who would want to play Phil Parker's defense and an offensive unit that moves the ball better than any Hawkeye version in years. Iowa shut out the Illini in the second half and backup RB L.J. Phillips, in for the injured Kamari Moulton, ran for 154 yards — this third straight 100-yard outing.

When in doubt, run QB Faizon Brandon. That's what the Vols did. He ran for 112 yards on just 12 carries — nearly 10 yards a pop — and scored two touchdowns in the fourth quarter. It was more than enough for Tennessee to re-enter our Top 10 ahead of a big game in Nashville next week. Win and they're (likely) in the postseason.

articles.title: Tony Pulis column: How does Mauricio Pochettino prepare for his first Man Utd game?
articles.summary: BBC Sport columnist Tony Pulis explains how new Manchester United boss Mauricio Pochettino will prepare for Sunday's game against Liverpool after only a few days with his squad.
articles.body:
Stepping into a job like Mauricio Pochettino has done at Manchester United , where managers have come and gone frequently, will always lead you to wonder why the others have not lasted very long.

Irrespective of results, you face these first few days in your new post with suspicion.

So, while what happens in Pochettino's first game against Liverpool on Sunday is important, it will not define his early opinions of the club - good or bad.

Whenever you take over a team in mid-season, which I did on a few occasions, you don't usually get much time to work with your players before your first game.

Jumping straight in and going straight to the heart of a two-day preparation for a game, like Pochettino has done before United go to Anfield, is so difficult and I am not sure any manager can honestly make a profound difference.

A change of voice helps, I'm sure, but so does showing strength and confidence in your own principles and making sure the players understand you demand complete and utter commitment in all the games you face, starting with this one.

With time on the training ground being so limited, my initial work would focus on us being a team and working up and down the pitch together, by breaking down different scenarios inside the game and what we should do in them.

I'd keep the focus on hard work and making us difficult to beat - clean sheets are so under-rated.

Then, on the day, your first pre-match speech is always a massive one, and it will be the same for Pochettino too.

My first team talk would always focus on generating an 'us against the world' mentality. As a manager coming in now, you've usually got the job because the team has struggled, so you can play on that to motivate the players.

You can use media reports and stories to show the negativity against them - but then counter that by producing a real 'stand-up and be counted' kind of rallying call, before sending them out on the pitch, while mentioning your faith in them to succeed.

'What your own eyes tell you is most important'

I would have selected my team before I met the players, through my own knowledge and also with help from within.

Whichever club I went in at, I'd expect to know something about most of the players within the group in terms of their position and ability, but understanding the character of the squad was vital too.

The existing staff would know more about the lads' qualities in that respect than myself or anyone who had just arrived with me, so I'd always discuss that with the people I had inherited, from fitness coaches to the medical department.

It's what your own eyes tell you that is most important, however. Going into your first game gives you the opportunity to see for yourself what your players are made of - and it can be a completely different view from what other people see.

Most of the early games I managed would be hit and miss in terms of selection, but I would quickly work out the strengths and weaknesses of the group.

As I've mentioned in previous columns, one of my first aims at any club where I was manager was about putting out a team, not a group of individuals.

It does not take long to see when that is not happening. I can remember my first game of my first spell at Stoke, a 4-2 defeat at Walsall in the Championship.

I wasn't universally enamoured by certain crowd favourites in that team and, while any manager knows that leaving some of them out could have an adverse effect on the supporters' view of yourself, you have to stand up and make decisions based on what you see.

It is the same if there are other issues with the squad you have inherited too.

West Brom's first game after I was appointed manager was a draw with West Ham on New Year's Day 2015.

I sat in the stands at Upton Park with my son, Anthony, who was concerned how different the Albion team was compared to Crystal Palace , the last team I had managed in the Premier League.

He was right to worry about it, but we still found a way - a totally different way of playing, but still a way to win that suited the group.

All your staff have to understand your objectives

My initial aims after arriving at any club mid-season were pretty direct and also pretty basic too.

The staff I inherited did not just know the players, they were also the first group who had to understand my objectives and also my principles - like the work ethic I expected, for example.

Irrespective of what they were used to doing, it was imperative they followed my lead.

One of the clubs I arrived at were struggling at the foot of the table and also suffering from a glut of injuries.

In my opinion, the players were taking advantage of a very honest and hard-working medical department, who were quite accommodating on the treatment times for the lads.

I changed that immediately, so injured players were treated at 9am, 2pm and 4pm, with sessions in-between those times for strength and recovery workouts.

This did not go down well with the players because it impeded on their social lives and, in one case, a player whose injury record was not exactly brilliant came to me complaining that his wife expected him to pick his children up from school and being asked to be in at 4pm affected his private life too.

I did not budge, and funnily enough the player in question recovered quite quickly - as did the majority of the other injured players.

'Not the right time' - Fernandes pauses Man Utd contract talks

Cost of Man Utd hiring and firing managers nears £100m

'Clear the treatment rooms, and make sure the players are fit'

Asking injured players to be at the training ground all day was by far the best way of getting them fit, in my experience, and the medical departments I managed were all working well past 4pm anyway so it was no hardship to them.

Just on that side of things, I would sometimes get the feeling some medical departments thought that, if they weren't treating players, then they weren't doing their jobs.

That was completely the opposite to how I saw it. I would congratulate people for having empty treatment rooms and applaud them for their work.

Treatment rooms are comfort areas that certain players would always gravitate to, to have a kiss and a cuddle if they are feeling sorry for themselves for not being in the team. That's one of the first things that has to change, because you cannot give your players any excuses or hiding places if they are not performing.

Similarly, I have always laughed at new managers who take over in mid-season and complain about the lack of fitness in their squad.

I am sure I have done it myself at some point, but then I had a reputation of managing extremely fit squads of players and it was always an area I studied really closely.

Early on in my management career, we weren't blessed with the advanced fitness equipment used in football today, but I was still able to quickly arrive at the level I believed the players should be at.

Firstly, I had my own fitness runs that were tried and tested but, also, I knew that if during a fitness session they weren't moaning and sweating, they weren't working hard enough.

Privately, you can realise very quickly when and which additions to the squad are needed.

Pochettino will no doubt be thinking about that at United already, but he has 10 games in the Premier League and Champions League before the January transfer window opens.

In the meantime, everything has to be geared towards winning games. I always knew I needed to do that quickly, because it helps the players believe in what I was doing, which is important too.

I've outlined my principles I held at every club above, and they never changed, but my playing principles were determined by the quality of the group I inherited.

My big strength as a coach was relaying what I needed from every individual player in the team, and I'm afraid repeated sessions were the go-to remedy to get there.

I apologise to all the lads who had to put up with me barking out the same commands, day after day, until even our weaker links would remember their individual and the team's plays in and out of possession.

'Bounce or not, future recruitment is key'

It goes without saying that with United changing their manager again, their supporters will be hoping for an immediate bounce in respect of results and performance.

Michael Carrick's results when he took the reins at Old Trafford at the start of this year were fantastic, with six wins and a draw in his first seven league games - including victories over Manchester City and Arsenal .

As a consequence, he steered United from mid-table to third place and Champions League qualification.

Even if Pochettino delivers something similar then, for that success to last, he has to be able to have more control over the future recruitment into the club.

That has been an absolute disaster recently, and I don't believe blame for it can be thrown in Carrick's direction.

In fact, Pochettino should use what has happened as his argument for what needs to change to achieve his aims of bringing United out of recession and on the road to recovery.

Tony Pulis was speaking to BBC Sport's Chris Bevan.

articles.title: El susto de Leandro Paredes: cayó redondo al suelo tras desmayarse en plena entrevista
articles.standfirst: El capitán de Boca sufrió un golpe de calor mientras atendía a un periodista
articles.summary: El capitán de Boca sufrió un golpe de calor mientras atendía a un periodista
articles.body: Leandro Paredes, capitán de Boca Juniors, se desmayó este sábado tras los festejos del título de la Copa Sudamericana al sufrir una descompensación a raíz de las altas temperaturas en Barranquilla que forzaron su temprana salida del juego ante Atlético Mineiro. El mediocampista, campeón del Mundial de Catar 2022 con Argentina, se desmayó mientras hablaba con un periodista de DSports y quedó tendido en el túnel del estadio ante el susto de todos los presentes. Paredes fue auxiliado de inmediato y recibió asistencia médica ante el inesperado suceso. El capitán de Boca sufrió un fuerte golpe de calor debido a las altas temperaturas (cerca de 30°C con 80 % de humedad y casi 39°C de sensación térmica) sumado al desgaste físico tras recuperarse recientemente de un desgarro. Afortunadamente, pocos segundos después, el capitán xeneize logró reincoporarse y se dirigió por sus propios medios al vestuario de su equipo en el estadio Metropolitano Roberto Meléndez, de Barranquilla. Durante el partido, Paredes pidió el cambio a los 58 minutos por ahogo y agotamiento extremo, momento en el que sus compañeros Adam Bareiro y Rodrigo Battaglia tuvieron que abanicarlo con sus camisetas y aplicarle hielo en el banco de suplentes. En su conferencia de prensa posterior, Rodolfo Arruabarrena brindó tranquilidad al hablar del estado de Paredes. "Ahí lo cruce entrando al vestuario, es verdad que terminando el primer tiempo tuvo un bajón y se sentía cansado. En el entretiempo mejoró un poco pero a los diez minutos se veía que le costaba trasladar a los costados. Es muy honesto y pidió el cambio, recién me enteré que ahora le había pasado un bajón", afirmó 'el Vasco'.

articles.title: No. 17 Boise State suffers costly loss to San Diego State after late clock-management snafu
articles.summary: Boise State's playoff hopes took a big hit.
articles.body:
San Diego State hit a field goal as time expired to beat No. 17 Boise State 22-20 in a stunning upset Saturday night on Boise's famed blue turf.

Cooper DiLeva's winning 42-yard kick deals a serious blow to Boise's College Football Playoff hopes, which it could earn by finishing the season as the highest-ranked Group of Six team. The Broncos (9-2) are by no means out of playoff contention, and will still play for the Pac-12 title in two weeks, but the loss opens the door for another G6 contender.

SDSU's victory was made possible by a bizarre sequence in the final minutes as the Broncos were trying to run out the clock with the ball.

On third-and-8 with 1:41 on the clock, BSU threw a pass that ended up with tight end Keawe Browne out of bounds, which stopped the clock at 1:36. The Aztecs had zero timeouts so that was a huge favor.

On the next play, fourth-and-3 at the SDSU 45-yard line, BSU tried for the first down rather than punting and pinning back the Aztecs. Quarterback Maddux Madsen was stuffed for a loss, giving SDSU the ball in prime field position with 1:31 left on the clock.

The Aztecs (6-5) quickly drove into field-goal range to set up the winning kick.

SDSU QB Stone Saunders played a part in both of his team's touchdowns, scoring on a 9-yard run in the third quarter and throwing a 39-yard scoring pass to Jaylon Hawkins with 1:58 to play.

San Diego could have tied it with a PAT at that point but opted to go for 2 and came up short. That gave Boise State the ball with a 20-19 lead and under two minutes to play, but the Broncos weren't able to close out the victory.

articles.title: Bruno Fernandes: Man Utd captain confirms contract offer but says negotiations are on hold
articles.summary: Bruno Fernandes speaks exclusively to Sky Sports about his Man Utd future after rejecting two contract offers, insisting he will leave if the club want him to go; watch Liverpool vs Manchester United live on Sky Sports Main Event from 4pm, kick-off at 4.30pm.
articles.body:
Fernandes has rejected two contract offers from United , Sky Sports News understands, with his current deal due to expire at the end of the season. The club's initial proposal was made in the summer when discussions first began over a new deal, but was turned down by the Portuguese, who signed his last contract in August 2024.

United hold an option to extend the 32-year-old's stay at Old Trafford by a further year, which would also prevent him from speaking to foreign clubs in January over the possibility of a free transfer.

The United captain, who has repeatedly been linked with a move away from Old Trafford, confirmed an offer has been made but dismissed suggestions that negotiations are ongoing or that he has demanded more money or an extended deal.

Fernandes also made clear he would not stand in the club's way if they decided his future lay elsewhere, insisting he has always prioritised United and would not simply stay to run down his contract.

Asked for an update on his contract situation ahead of Manchester United's clash with Liverpool, live on Sky Sports on Super Sunday from 4pm (kick-off at 4.30pm), Fernandes said: "No, there's no negotiations ongoing, but I've seen people saying that he's asked for more money, he's asked for more years. If I wanted more money, I wouldn't be here. I had somewhere to go to get much more money than being at Manchester United.

"I could have been in a place that is much warmer than Manchester.

"Two summers ago, three summers ago, last summer, I always had the chance to leave and I always chose to be here. The thing is, I've always showed how much I care about the club and how much I want to win at this club. And I always said, in the moment the club thinks it's time for me to move on, I will move on.

"I'm not going to be the player that I've seen many in this time at Manchester United. They're going to stay here just by staying, just finish my contract and then we will see. In the moment the club says, 'Bruno, it's time to part ways', I'm going to be the first one walking out the door.

"Yeah, the club offered me a new contract, so I think that, from their side, shows that they want me to stay. And as you said, there are no negotiations going on.

"We spoke about the contract at the end of last season, we came in the beginning of this season speaking about the contract, but about the context of the team and the club, I just put that to a side because I don't think it's the right moment, neither for me, nor for the club, to be talking about negotiations because the most important thing now is that the club gets back to win games."

'I still want to win Premier League and Champions League with Man Utd'

Fernandes insists his ambitions at United have not changed, despite the club's struggles, and remains determined to bring major honours back to Old Trafford.

"My aim will always be to win the Premier League and the Champions League within the club I am," he said.

The midfielder refused to accept that simply qualifying for the Champions League should become United's primary target. "I will never hide from that, I will never say, no, our position at the moment needs to be to get top four."

Fernandes acknowledged winning the Premier League this season was likely to be beyond United but insisted that was not his expectation when the campaign began.

He also believes supporters have been too patient with the club, recognising their frustration after years without a league title.

"They've been far too patient with us," he said.

'There was never a problem with Carrick'

Fernandes dismissed suggestions of a breakdown in his relationship with former United boss, Michael Carrick, following his comments during an interview after a 4-1 defeat to Como last month and his subsequent spell on the bench.

The United captain revealed Carrick had personally explained his decision to leave him out against Bournemouth, insisting it had nothing to do with his interview.

"The manager came to speak to me after that game, or before the Bournemouth game, to say, 'look, I'm not going to start you tomorrow' and everything.

"There's nothing to do with the words of Como, I know people will make it around that. I just want to tell you that we need to change something, I need to make a change, performances have not been great, so I just want you to know that there's nothing to do with that," Fernandes said.

He added that he subsequently approached Carrick to clear up any potential misunderstanding, with the manager reassuring him there was no personal issue.

"I told him, 'I think that you probably got our words in the wrong way, and you might be upset with me, and rightly so, if you got it in the way everyone is speaking about it'. And he said, 'Bruno, I'm not; I just put you on the bench because I thought it was the best for the team'."

Fernandes said his return to the starting XI the following game was further evidence that there had been no fallout between the pair.

'Pochettino brings good, positive energy'

Fernandes offered a positive early assessment of new United manager Mauricio Pochettino after beginning work with him.

The captain described the new boss as energetic and demanding, revealing Pochettino had already made clear the standards he expects from his players.

"He's someone that likes to bring a very good energy to the team, someone very positive, very strong, strict, said it straight away that he won't allow us to not give him what he demands from the team, from each player," Fernandes said.

"He wants the club to succeed so much, he wants to win games, and that's pretty clear and obvious by the way he and his staff speak and want us to improve."

Fernandes revealed he came close to joining Tottenham in 2019 when Pochettino was in charge at the north London club.

The midfielder confirmed he met with Tottenham's board, who outlined how he could fit into the manager's system, with the prospect of playing alongside Harry Kane, Dele Alli and Heung-Min Son proving attractive.

"Obviously I was a very young player that was eager to come to the Premier League. They had Kane there, they had Dele Alli, Son, the chance of playing with those players in front was very attractive," he said.

articles.title: Leandro Paredes: Argentina midfielder collapses during TV interview
articles.summary: World Cup winning midfielder Leandro Paredes collapses while giving a post-match interview minutes after winning a trophy with Boca Juniors.
articles.body:
World Cup winning midfielder Leandro Paredes collapsed while giving a post-match interview minutes after winning a trophy with Boca Juniors.

The former Paris St-Germain midfielder, 32, was suffering with the heat and humidity in Barranquilla, Colombia, where Boca won the Copa Sudamericana by beating Atletico Mineiro of Brazil 2-0.

He was replaced during the second half, then collapsed while being interviewed on television, with pictures showing a journalist trying to break his fall.

After some treatment Argentine Paredes was able to walk to the dressing room and joined in with his team's celebrations.

"Thanks to everyone for the messages, it was just dizziness," he said on Instagram , external after the match.

Heat was a discussion before the game with forecasts predicting tempertures could reach 32C and humidity around 80%.

Boca manager Rodolfo Arruabarrena said he noticed the midfielder's difficulties during the second half.

"He felt dizzy towards the end of the first half," Arruabarrena said.

"He improved a little during the break, but after 10 minutes in the second half you could see he was struggling."

Paredes started his career with Boca before moving to Europe in 2015.

The victory for Boca ended an 18-year international trophy drought for the Argentine side.

By securing their 19th international cup, Boca also became South America's most decorated club since 1960, overtaking domestic rivals Independiente who have 18.

articles.title: Women's Super League: Why Arsenal are behind in race for Champions League places
articles.summary: Arsenal were open about their aim to win the WSL this season but they find themselves well adrift - where have things gone wrong?
articles.body:
Before the 2026-27 season began, Arsenal technical director Jodie Taylor declared: "I'll flat out say it: we want to win the league and want to take that next step."

After finishing second last season, it seemed like a logical statement to make.

However, after 10 games in this season's Women's Super League, they are sixth in the table, trailing leaders Chelsea by 13 points.

They are also nine points behind third-placed London City Lionesses, albeit with a game in hand, and facing stiff competition to qualify for the Champions League again next campaign.

BBC Sport looks at where things have gone wrong for the Gunners, who have not won the WSL since 2018-19.

Last term, Arsenal hosted all 11 of their league home games at Emirates Stadium for the first time, winning eight times and drawing on three occasions.

This season, Renee Slegers' side have drawn all five of their home games and will seek their first win at the sixth attempt when they host West Ham on Sunday (14:30 GMT), live on BBC Two.

Two of those draws came against promoted sides Crystal Palace and Birmingham City, where a combined 57 shots yielded just one goal.

Home fans are getting disgruntled and this has been reflected in attendances. Last season, the Gunners had an average attendance of 33,808, better than eight Premier League clubs.

So far this year their biggest crowd was against London City Lionesses last weekend, when 32,588 were in the stands.

Speaking on the Women's Football Weekly podcast, former England striker Ellen White said: "The Emirates seems [like] a bit of an issue for them at the moment - they just can't get that win there.

"A draw might feel like a loss for them because they are so far behind now in terms of the Champions League spots."

Former Gunners striker Vivianne Miedema, who did play at Emirates Stadium for Arsenal but joined Manchester City before the full switch was made, added: "Players always say that the crowd really, really helps you at Arsenal. The fans are amazing - it gives you that extra bit of energy.

"Obviously playing in the Emirates with all the fans should still give them that boost but it doesn't seem to be fully working for them this season so far."

Plenty of shots - but a lack of clinical edge

The Gunners have had 199 shots in 10 league matches but managed just 11 goals. That is just over one goal per game, and their conversion rate of 5.53% is the lowest of any club over the past six seasons.

Part of the problem could be an over-reliance on key goalscorer Alessia Russo.

She has alternated between the number nine and number 10 position during the season but thrives most when she is the focal point in the attack.

This season, the England striker has five league goals and provided two assists, with her form improving in recent weeks.

She was player of the match against Tottenham after scoring and providing an assist in a 2-1 win and similarly against Liverpool, when she scored twice to help Arsenal triumph by the same scoreline.

After Russo, only Lisa Baum (two), Georgia Stanway (two), Smilla Holmberg and Frida Maanum have scored in the league.

Injuries to attacking options Chloe Kelly, Selina Cerci and Stina Blackstenius have also proved costly, while key midfielder Mariona Caldentey is about halfway through an expected 10-week absence with a hamstring injury.

The result is that Arsenal and Brighton are the only teams in the league to have a goal difference of zero after 10 games.

Contrast that with title rivals Chelsea, who have scored 29 goals and have a goal difference of +24, while defending champions Manchester City have netted 27 times.

While Slegers will always be hailed for winning Arsenal's second Champions League title last year against Barcelona, questions have been asked about her future after another slow start to the season.

In three of their home league matches, Arsenal have fallen behind and dropped points. Last Sunday, they went ahead against London City but only held the lead for 98 seconds.

It was a big summer of change in north London with club stalwarts Katie McCabe and Beth Mead among those departing, and seven new signings arriving including Stanway, Cerci and Baum.

Also among the arrivals was Swiss midfielder Geraldine Reuteler, who helped her country reach the quarter-finals of Euro 2025 but has struggled for minutes since signing a four-year deal in the summer.

She has made just four appearances across all competitions, appearing for a total of just 66 minutes in the WSL.

The results have left Slegers vulnerable and a first home win of the season against West Ham would be a much-needed boost for a side that have fallen far short of the lofty targets they set back in September.

articles.title: Man Utd: Bruno Fernandes offered new deal but no talks are ongoing
articles.summary: Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes says he has been offered a new contract by the club but feels it "is not the right time" for discussions about his future.
articles.body:
Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes says he has been offered a new contract by the club but feels it "is not the right time" for discussions about his future.

The 32-year-old midfielder is out of contract at the end of the season , though the club have the option to trigger a 12-month extension until 2028.

He was left out of the side under previous manager Michael Carrick but says he has no issues at the club and has chosen to stay at Old Trafford despite offers elsewhere in recent seasons.

He told Sky Sports: , external "The club offered me a new contract, so I think that, from their side, shows that they want me to stay.

"There's no negotiations ongoing, but I've seen people saying that 'he's asked for more money, he's asked for more years'. If I wanted more money, I wouldn't be here.

"I had somewhere to go to get much more money than being at Manchester United. I could have been in a place that is much warmer than Manchester.

"Two summers ago, three summers ago, last summer, I always had the chance to leave and I always chose to be here."

United chief executive Omar Berrada recently spoke about Fernandes' contract situation, saying: "It's true that we're having conversations about his new contract, but I prefer to keep that private."

Fernandes has scored 75 Premier League goals since signing from Sporting in 2020 and last season set a record for the most assists in a Premier League season.

His form has tailed off this season in a poor start for the club as a whole.

United are 19th in the Premier League table going into Mauricio Pochettino's first game in charge against rivals Liverpool on Sunday afternoon.

"We spoke about the contract at the end of last season," Fernandes said.

"We came in at the beginning of this season speaking about the contract, but about the context of the team and the club, I just put that to a side because I don't think it's the right moment, neither for me, nor for the club, to be talking about negotiations.

"The most important thing now is that the club gets back to winning games."

Fernandes was dropped for the Premier League defeat by Bournemouth last month after being critical of United's approach in their heavy defeat against Como in the Champions League.

But Fernandes says he did not fall out with Carrick, who was sacked on 12 November.

"The manager came to speak to me before the Bournemouth game, to say: 'Look, I'm not going to start you tomorrow. There's nothing to do with the words of Como, I know people will make it around that. I just want to tell you that we need to change something, I need to make a change, performances have not been great, so I just want you to know that there's nothing to do with that'," Fernandes said.

articles.title: La frustración de Messi: pelotazo en la cara a un rival en la derrota del Inter Miami
articles.standfirst: El argentino le dio un pelotazo por considerar que Gonzalo Tapia, ex de River, intentaba perder tiempo en la goleada del Columbus Crew
articles.summary: El argentino le dio un pelotazo por considerar que Gonzalo Tapia, ex de River, intentaba perder tiempo en la goleada del Columbus Crew
articles.body: El Inter Miami perdió en la primera ronda de los 'playoffs' de la MLS ante el Columbus Crew por 0-3 en el Nu Stadium. El encuentro, en el que Leo Messi recibió un homenaje previo por conquistar una nueva Bota de Oro de la competición, estuvo marcado por la derrota y la frustración del argentino, que dio un pelotazo en la cara a Gonzalo Tapia por querer perder tiempo. La tensión de una primera mitad adversa estalló en el tiempo añadido, en el minuto 45+5', durante una acción con saque de banda a favor del conjunto de Florida. Cuando Messi intentaba reanudar el juego con rapidez, Gonzalo Tapia se colocó delante para obstruirlo y el capitán del Inter Miami reaccionó lanzándole el balón directamente a la cara, lo que derribó al delantero chileno. El árbitro Allen Chapman optó por saldar el incidente con tarjeta amarilla para ambos jugadores, evitando la expulsión del astro argentino, que es lo que pidieron los rivales, que en ese momento vencían por 0-1. En la segunda mitad, con inferioridad numérica por la expulsión de Lujan, el Inter Miami no logró reaccionar y el Columbus Crew amplió la brecha gracias al tanto de Taha Habroune en el minuto 52 y al doblete de Gonzalo Tapia en el 58', cerrando el 0-3 definitivo. Al disputarse la eliminatoria al mejor de tres encuentros, el equipo de Messi queda contra las cuerdas y obligado a ganar su próximo compromiso para forzar un tercer partido y evitar la eliminación en la primera ronda.

articles.title: Vinicius enciende la chispa y Espí mantiene la llama
articles.standfirst: El brasileño revolucionó el ataque y el español anotó su cuarto gol en 63’
articles.summary: El brasileño revolucionó el ataque y el español anotó su cuarto gol en 63’
articles.body: En realidad José Mourinho hizo lo que tocaba. El Real Madrid venía de sumar ocho victorias entre los dos parones internacionales, y en cuatro de ellos, los correspondientes a partidos de Liga, lo hizo con Yan Diomande como titular y ocupando la plaza que en teoría corresponde a Vinicius, sancionado con cuatro partidos tras su expulsión ante el Villarreal. El equipo respondió, con el costamarfileño rayando a gran nivel, a base de goles (algunos brillantes), y asistencias. El Madrid parecía, además, más equilibrado, ya que el ex del Leipzig destacaba también por su aportación en el aspecto defensivo, quizá la gran carencia de Vinicius. Así que Mou repitió ante el Celta con Yan en la banda izquierda. Y de nuevo estuvo bien, lúcido en el uno contra uno, aunque sus buenos centros no encontraron remates claros. Pero el Celta, que se había delantado muy pronto en el marcador, estaba conteniendo bien a un Madrid lento en el primer tiempo, sin que llegara el arrebato que siempre genera la cercanía del minuto 90. Y esta vez el toque de corneta lo protagonizó Vinicius, activado desde el banquillo por Mourinho, que entró en su sitio, desplazando a Diomande a la derecha. Allí perdió filo el mayor traspaso del verano, pero Vini lo compensó desde el otro costado. Apareció mucho y bien, fino en el regate, atrevido, algo que se había echado en falta en varios de sus últimos partidos, en los que encaró muy por debajo de su media. Ayer no. Ayer fue de nuevo el martillo pilón que lo intenta una y mil veces, salga bien o mal. Y la mayor parte de las veces salió bien. De hecho, apareció en la foto de los dos goles del Madrid. En el 1-1, con la arrancada que precedió al ligero toque de Mbappé para asistir a Bellingham. Y en el 2-1, para poner en la frente de Espí el balón que, tras el doble esfuerzo del delantero valenciano, dejó los tres puntos en el Bernabéu. Lo de Espi Lo de Espí es materia aparte. Ayer sumó su cuarto gol en poco más de una hora de juego, tres de ellos (Espanyol, Elche y Celta) para darle a su equipo tres victorias agónicas, y al mismo tiempo fundamentales para que el Madrid esté, antes de la conclusión de esta jornada, empatado a puntos con el líder. Ningún jugador de Europa ha logrado tantos goles como el ariete valenciano saliendo desde el banquillo, y con apenas una hora de juego. Son sólo 63 minutos para el internacional sub 21, que más allá de eso empieza a intimidar rivales: Cuando Espi sale, marca y el Madrid gana. Ya es casi matemático.

articles.title: El Real Madrid encontró el premio a su insistencia
articles.standfirst: Los blancos necesitaron 24 tiros y casi todo el territorio para alcanzar una victoria que parecía resistirse
articles.summary: Los blancos necesitaron 24 tiros y casi todo el territorio para alcanzar una victoria que parecía resistirse
articles.body: Parecía que el Celta iba a volver a sacar tajada en el Bernabéu un año después de su sorprendente triunfo. Anduvo cerca, porque se adelantó en el marcador y lo mantuvo durante muchos minutos. Pero el Real Madrid, tras un mal inicio, fue entrando en el partido hasta acabar dominándolo. Tardó en generar tiros a puerta e, incluso, falló un penalti. Sin embargo, acabó encontrando premio a su dominio avasallador como bien reflejan los números. El gol celeste llegó pronto y nació de una posesión larga y limpia: 15 pases y diez jugadores distintos en 35 segundos, una cadena que arrancó poco después de que Güler bloqueara un remate de Swedberg y que terminó con Durán, con la derecha y a 3,4 metros del centro de la portería, firmando el 0-1. A partir de ahí el partido tuvo un solo dueño, aunque el marcador tardó una hora en admitirlo. El Momentum refleja con claridad quién generó mayor peligro y de manera más continuada. El Real Madrid mereció más. El Celta solo generó mayor peligro en los minutos posteriores a su gol y en un breve repunte justo antes del empate, dos disparos en 80 segundos que fueron toda su reacción de la segunda parte. Durante tres cuartas partes del partido la iniciativa fue del Madrid, y sus dos picos más altos llegan después del empate, hacia el 71' y el 87', cuando el Celta ya no volvió a disparar. El Real Madrid dominó también territorialmente. La cuota de pases en el último tercio respecto del total del partido fue casi del 80% (en la segunda parte llegó al 87%), lo que denota un claro dominio en los metros finales. La segunda parte es la que mejor lo explica. El Madrid inició 136 pases en el último tercio; el Celta, 21. Con tan poco balón en campo contrario, los gallegos pasaron más de media hora de juego sin un solo disparo, del minuto 32 al 64, y cuando por fin tiraron lo hicieron dos veces seguidas, justo antes de encajar. Una buena prueba de ello fue que el Celta tuvo que achicar mucho agua durante el encuentro. Entre recuperaciones y despejes, sus jugadores intervinieron 67 veces (36 y 31, respectivamente), con Javi Rodríguez protagonizando 11 de ellos. El mapa concentra el partido en la mitad izquierda, la de su portería. De los 31 despejes, 29 se hicieron en su tercio defensivo y ninguno en el tercio ofensivo. Las recuperaciones siguen la misma pauta, 22 de 36 en el primer tercio, con una altura media de 38 metros desde su portería. Y cuando el balón no se despejaba, el juego se cortaba con faltas: 13, frente a las 4 del Madrid. Con el balón casi siempre en campo celeste, al Madrid le sobraron los tiros y le faltó acierto. Llegar al área, llegaba: 16 de sus 24 disparos salieron desde dentro, por 5 del Celta. Pero uno de cada tres acabó bloqueado (8 de 24), mientras que el Celta solo vio taponado uno de sus ocho. La primera parte lo resume. Doce tiros, solo dos a puerta y ningún gol, con un penalti de Mbappé mandado por encima del larguero en el minuto 39. La manera de intentar tampoco parecía la correcta. El Madrid centró 27 veces en juego y solo 6 llegaron a un compañero, un 22% que resume lo poco que sirvió el recurso. Ninguno de esos centros acabó siendo asistencia oficial. Hay un tramo que condensa el problema. Del 48:28 al 65:31, 17 minutos, el Madrid no disparó ni una vez. En ese vacío, dentro de la segunda parte con más pases en campo rival, lanzó 11 centros, completó 2 y ninguno acabó en tiro. Los tres cambios del 57, con Vinicius entre ellos, cayeron en mitad de ese desierto, y el primer disparo posterior fue el del empate. Cambió el panorama y el Madrid vio en el premio una victoria que merecía. El reparto por carriles encaja con esa imagen. El Madrid ensanchó el ataque mientras el Celta despejaba todo lo que caía en su área, y por dentro se entró poco. La izquierda fue por donde más entró el balón al último tercio, casi la mitad de los pases completados hacia esa zona, que es por donde llegaron los dos goles blancos. . El empate llegó en el 66' y se parece muy poco al resto del partido: cuatro jugadores, unos 14 segundos y ningún centro. Güler, Vinicius y Mbappé, autor del pase, dejaron a Bellingham rematar desde la frontal, de cara al centro de la portería, 35 segundos después del último disparo del Celta con una mano salvadora de Courtois. Los gallegos no volvieron a tirar. El 2-1 sí llegó por el camino que el Madrid había recorrido tantas veces. Era el centro número 26 del partido. Vinicius, que había entrado en el 57' y estaba también en el empate, puso el balón en el área a Espí, en el campo desde el 79', que ganó el duelo aéreo. Radu le paró el remate y el rechace lo empujó él mismo. Los números daban la razón al Madrid en el juego y el marcador acabó dándosela también. Los blancos encontraron el empate por un camino y la victoria por otro. La insistencia tuvo premio y los tres puntos se quedaron en el Bernabéu.

articles.title: Ian Watson: Rochdale sack head coach Ian Watson with club 22nd in League Two
articles.summary: Rochdale sack head coach Ian Watson after only five months at the League Two club
articles.body:
Rochdale have sacked head coach Ian Watson after only five months in charge of the League Two club.

The former South Shields boss replaced promotion-winning manager Jimmy McNulty in June after he joined Stockport but leaves the club just two points clear of the relegation zone.

Watson took South Shields to the National League North play-off final last season where they were beaten by Kidderminster Harriers before taking up his first Football League role at Spotland.

After returning to the EFL by beating Boreham Wood in last season's National League promotion final, Rochdale have won only four of their 16 League Two matches so far this season.

He departs following Saturday's 3-2 defeat by Northampton Town which was their fourth successive loss and left them 22nd in the table.

"We would like to thank Ian for his hard work and commitment during his time at the Crown Oil Arena and wish him every success in the future," said a club statement. , external

"The process to appoint a successor is already underway, and the club will give a further update in due course."

Rochdale are next in action at home to Barnet on Saturday, 28 November (15:00 GMT).

articles.title: El Betis denuncia insultos racistas a Natan y la mujer de Valles amenazas contra su hija
articles.standfirst: El defensa fue increpado cuando se dirigía al bus del equipo y la mujer del portero denuncia que desde los Biris desearon la muerte de su hija
articles.summary: El defensa fue increpado cuando se dirigía al bus del equipo y la mujer del portero denuncia que desde los Biris desearon la muerte de su hija
articles.body: El Betis y el Sevilla empataron este sábado en el derbi sevillano. No hubo grandes contratiempos en el campo, pero sí en la grada. Durante y después del encuentro. Desde el cuadro bético se denuncian insultos racistas a Natan cuando se dirigía al bus y la mujer de Álvaro Valles quiso denunciar las amenazas que recibía el portero hacia su hija. Entre las expresiones dirigidas al defensa bético se escucharon gritos como. "Negro, a mamarla, Natan, negro, a chuparla, los huevos pa' dentro. Mucho Betis, mucha mierda", según desvelaba El Desmarque. Natan continuó su camino sin detenerse y posteriormente respondió a través de X, centrando su mensaje en el próximo compromiso europeo del equipo, el partido de Champions del martes ante el Slovan en Bratislava: "Tranquilo, que el negro está centrado en el partido del martes, seguimos mi Betis". Por otro lado, María Saravia, mujer de Álvaro Valles, denunció los gritos contra su hija. Colgó su denuncia en su cuenta de Instagram, donde explicó que había sucedido durante el calentamiento antes del partido cuando el guardameta se ejercía frente a la grada de los Biris, los ultras del Sevilla. Allí escuchó: "Ojalá se muera tu hija esta noche". Este es el mensaje íntegro que María Saravia publicó en su cuenta de Instagram: “Hoy mientras mi marido calentaba antes de empezar el derbi en la portería de los Biris, un hombre (por llamarlo de alguna forma) le ha dicho a mi marido que ojalá se muera su hija esta noche. Nunca jamás he entrado al trapo, porque el fútbol a fin de cuentas siempre tiene rivalidad y a veces es hasta bonito. Pero el mal nacido, escoria, poco hombre, mala persona, indeseable, con maldad, sinvergüenza y con poca educación de tiparraco que le ha deseado eso a mi hija, porque la hija del portero es la mía, QUIERO DECIRTE QUE LO QUE LE DESEES A LA HIJA DEL PORTERO, MI HIJA, TE DESEO YO A TI LO MISMO MULTIPLICADO POR 10. Que ojalá llegues a leer esto y me contestes. Para meterse con una criatura hay que tener una bajeza humana que supera cualquier límite. Eres un miserable, un cobarde y una persona con una carencia de valores que da auténtica vergüenza. Y lo peor es que esto lo has hecho de la mano de un niño pequeño, sinvergüenza. Ojalá este texto lo llegues a leer y me contestes para ponerte cara, no entre hablar entre 40.000 personas”. Dada la gravedad de los hechos, las autoridades arbitrales puede que estudien el caso y tomen medidas.

articles.title: Alessio Dionisi: Watford sack boss after 18 games
articles.summary: Watford sack head coach Alessio Dionisi after 18 games in charge.
articles.body:
Watford are looking for their sixth manager in 18 months after they sacked head coach Alessio Dionisi following 18 games in charge.

The 46-year-old Italian was appointed in June after the departure of Ed Still, who himself lasted only three months at Vicarage Road.

Still, Javi Gracia and Paulo Pezzolano were all also given full-time contracts after Tom Cleverley left in May 2025.

Dionisi was Watford's 12th head coach, not including interim bosses, since the end of the 2020-21 season, and leaves the Hornets searching for a 25th since the Pozzo family took over the club in 2012.

The club have had 57 permanent managers in their 145-year history.

The decision to replace him comes after Saturday's crushing 4-0 defeat by Sheffield United at Bramall Lane.

Dionisi's dismissal caps an underwhelming start to the season, with the Hornets having won just four league games to leave them 21st in the table.

"We thank Alessio and his staff for his professionalism and their efforts," sporting director Luke Dowling told the club website. , external

"As I'm sure the supporters have seen, Alessio is a really good guy and we wish him the best for the future.

"The process has started for a replacement and we hope to be in a position to announce that shortly."

Dionisi was sacked by Serie B club Empoli in March after only five months in charge following a run of five wins in 22 matches.

His spell in charge of the Hornets was his first outside his homeland and started promisingly when his youthful side beat Southampton in their opening league game.

But they won only two of their next 12 in all competitions, and despite deservedly beating Charlton on 17 October, reverses at Wolves and Norwich followed, before four points from Dionisi's final three games in charge of the Hertfordshire side and his dismissal means further upheaval for the Hornets.

Since sacking Cleverley at the end of the 2024-25 campaign, the club has now been through four permanent head coaches, as well as interim boss Charlie Daniels' two-game spell in charge.

Of those four, only Gracia, in his second spell at Vicarage Road, took charge of more than 20 games.

On the morning of their final-day drubbing by Coventry last season, chief executive Scott Duxbury wrote a statement on the club website saying Watford had made mistakes, labelling their end to the campaign "unacceptable" and "truly disappointing in the extreme".

articles.title: Day after: Final thoughts on Notre Dame’s controlled 24-3 win over SMU
articles.summary: Notre Dame football got a solid win over SMU on Senior Day, and here are my final thoughts on the Irish’s 24-3 win over the Mustangs.
articles.body:
Notre Dame football got a solid win on Senior Day against SMU, 24-3 , as the defense was the star of the night.

Multiple stops inside the red zone slowed down the Mustangs enough for a fairly comfortable win to improve to 10-1. The Irish will now wait to see where they'll land in the next College Football Playoff rankings , with just two more to go until the final seeds are set.

Next week will be the last regular season game for Notre Dame, but let's wrap up the win over SMU. Here are my final thoughts on the Irish's Senior Day win over the Mustangs.

Was this Notre Dame performance a College Football Playoff-championship worthy effort?

The final score is a no, but this was a very good effort by the Irish. Notre Dame couldn't get its offense going all night, but still gained over 400-yards of total offense. The defense gave up a good amount of yards, but allowed just 3 points all night. As I said immediately after the game, this wasn't scoreboard pleasing, but it was a fully controlled victory for the Irish.

Thrust into a starting role, the former walk-on was one of the best players on an elite Notre Dame defense. Losing him to what looks like the rest of the year is heartbreaking. Talich is the kind of player that its easy to root for, one that had to earn everything he's gotten and has made the most of it. Hopefully this doesn't have an impact on his football future, as he played himself into potentially getting drafted.

Joey O'Brien's first extended look was very good results but …

The targeting penalty was a freshman mistake. You just can't lead with your head anymore. The crowd didn't like it and rightfully so, as captain Drayk Bowen came over to calm him down. He was the leading tackler when disqualified late in the fourth, and his impact was felt while he was in making tackles-for-losses and breaking up passes. Sans the targeting, this seemed like his Kyle Hamilton-moment.

Jordan Faison has been massively underrated

I don't think that Faison has gotten enough credit for how good he had been during his Irish career. He surpassed 2,000 career receiving yards against SMU, making him the No. 14 Notre Dame wide receiver all-time to pass that mark. All-American and National Champion lacrosse player, and could double-dip and win a football title this year. Faison is one of the all-time great Irish athletes.

Jaden Greathouse's injury complicates Notre Dame's wide receiver room

The Irish already had issues with its receiving core, and now that Greathouse got hurt, it puts even more doubt into the unit. Micah Gilbert had a solid game, Faison was great but no other receiver caught a pass. This could become an issues if Notre Dame faces a defense that can take away Faison, then others will have to step up. No one else has really shown they can be trusted at this point in the season. The lack of receiver depth could come back to haunt the Irish later in the postseason.

Charles Jagusah finally gets back on the field

A feel-good story, as Jagusah has been on the team since 2023, but had never played in Notre Dame stadium due to a variety of injuries. The team saw him working hard to get back onto the field and finally seeing the fruits of his labor being paid off on Saturday was huge for him and his teammates. Even though it was just a few snaps, it was great to see Jagusah back on the field.

articles.title: The Rafa Benitez curse Xabi Alonso could suffer if Chelsea don’t find an identity
articles.summary: Alonso is under growing pressure as Chelsea were booed by their own fans after their drubbing by Leeds
articles.body:
As the half-time whistle blew on another dire afternoon for Chelsea , boos emanated from parts of Stamford Bridge. They were on level terms with Leeds at this point; it was about to get a hell of a lot worse for the Blues fans in attendance as they watched their team, playing without purpose, get overrun.

The outpouring of anger from what was left of the home support was far more unanimous an hour or so later. Leeds had run out 4 - 1 victors , a scoreline that frankly flattered Chelsea. Barring a flash of brilliance from Emmanuel Emegha for the opener, the hosts had been absolutely outclassed - and it hadn't looked particularly laborious for the visitors. Like Tottenham fans a month earlier, the travelling Leeds contingent found themselves "ole-ing" at their opponents' expense, enjoying total control at a ground they hadn't previously won at this century.

Chelsea were embarrassed in a grudge match, again - and patience feels like it is really beginning to run thin. "I understand their disappointment for sure and we share that with them and whatever we can do is work, try to give our best to turn it back and to do much better," Xabi Alonso said. He is fighting fires three months into the season.

This is a fourth defeat in five for Alonso, a run that started with the sacrilegious home defeat to Spurs . That sort of result turned the fanbase against Antonio Conte in 2018, less than a year after he'd guided them to the title - so it was imperative for Alonso to regroup his side quickly in order to avoid meeting the same end.

That he has not done. Victory over a pitiful Manchester United team aside, Chelsea have failed to come close to inspiring in recent weeks. And now, amid this atrocious run of form, they actually have more Premier League losses to their name than crisis-ridden United. "We are in a fragile moment mentally," admitted Alonso, whose side is spiralling down the table.

The team looks systemically lost. In defence, Alonso has flip-flopped between a back three and back four on a gamely basis, though the confusion doesn't seem like it's hindering Chelsea's opposition more than it does themselves. They are persistently look open and passive - and against a team like Leeds, they were bullied, just as they were against Sunderland . This goes for their midfield, too, especially without Moises Caicedo - who was withdrawn through injury midway through the first half.

And things aren't much better going forward. What was initially touted as one of the most dangerous front threes in the league has turned toothless. The absence of Joao Pedro continues to be painfully detrimental, with Chelsea missing what he offers in the build-up along with his clinical finish. For parts of the first half, it felt like Emegha might be the solution Alonso has been searching for, finally playing a natural No 9 after three league matches of opting for alternatives. But the Dutchman faded and Chelsea ended the game with just an xG of 0.56.

Before the visit of Leeds, Alonso said: "I always know my best team for the next game we have." It's how he justified making the second most line-up changes of any other manager in the top-flight: 24. That rose to 28 on Saturday afternoon, and the result that followed confirmed that Alonso is still some way off finding his best team, or at least one with a clear identity.

This is obviously a cause for concern, because the Chelsea job is not known for having much of a grace period. The club's reactionary ownership and culture of change is an occupational hazard that Alonso would have been fully aware of when he put pen to paper last Spring. But usually , the fanbase is more forgiving, especially in early days of a project.

One notable exception to this comes to mind, though. The interim appointment of Rafa Benitez in 2012, replacing fan favourite Roberto Di Matteo , was met with chagrin due to his Liverpool past. Fans never took to the Spaniard, even after he led them to the Europa League title and a third-place finish. His tenure was ultimately short-lived, with his rival Jose Mourinho preferred the following summer.

As Chelsea's form metastasises, this buried anti-Liverpool sentiment is beginning to effervesce at the surface. Discontent towards the team could not even wait until full-time against Leeds, and fingers are being pointed at the manager.

Alonso arrived with a certain aura, the Spanish footballing mastermind that had turned Bayer Leverkusen into Bundesliga invincibles just two years earlier. But the honeymoon period is over; Alonso now must produce results to prevent it from boiling over, and risk falling to the same fate as his countryman and former boss.

Chelsea welcome Liverpool in three weeks' time, a fixture which could determine whether Alonso sinks or swims with the fans. He deserves to be given the time to correct the chaos on the pitch - but as far as morale goes, he cannot afford more disappointment in front of his own supporters against an arch-rival, not least his first English love. It remains to be seen whether this relationship is salvageable.
