articles.body:
The Cincinnati football Bearcats have mentally drained their fan base this season. They severed considerable trust after allowing a combined 79 points in road losses versus Arizona and West Virginia, revitalized alumni with a massive 37-24 victory over Texas Tech and then eventually stomped on people's hopes yet again after suffering a humiliating 41-13 defeat at Iowa State. Emotions are conflicted once more following Saturday's hard-earned 35-28 win against Colorado.

Cincy is now bowl-eligible and could further elevate its stock with a stunner versus BYU in the regular season finale. Bearcats head coach Scott Satterfield has stagnated, but upsetting a second College Football Playoff-caliber squad would certainly earn him points with fans. Achieving the same level of success as the pre-Big 12 era will be mighty difficult, at least for now. An eight-win campaign would qualify as visible progress.

Cincinnati inched closer to that benchmark after holding off Colorado in Nippert Stadium. JC French IV completed a spectacular 18-of-19 passes for 208 yards and two touchdowns. He rushed for another score. Cole Tabb had quite the day on the ground himself, registering 23 carries for 120 yards and two TDs. The defense deserves its shine, too, though.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

MJ Cannon, Kenny Worthy and Jasper Beeler each recorded an interception off Buffaloes quarterback Isaac Wilson, and Antwan Peek Jr. forced a fumble that was recovered by Beeler. In a game where both teams produced 433 yards of offense, a 4-1 turnover advantage proved to be critical.

Cincinnati football will need to make plenty more plays if it is going to prevail in Provo next Saturday. Bowl eligibility is not enough. Scott Satterfield understands the importance of this opportunity. He cannot allow his players to get complacent.

The Bearcats are not going to sniff the 2026 CFP, but they can do the next best thing. Eliminate a conference opponent from consideration. Then, a formerly disappointing season will turn into a mixed bag that features some incredible highs.

articles.title: Andoni Iraola Delivers Fresh Hugo Ekitike Injury Update as Liverpool Striker Targets January Return
articles.summary: Liverpool fans have been handed fresh hope over Hugo Ekitike’s injury comeback, with Andoni Iraola revealing a potential January return date.
articles.body:
Liverpool supporters have been handed a fresh update on Hugo Ekitike 's recovery, with Andoni Iraola remaining optimistic that the French forward could return to action in January as they prepare for a crucial period in their Champions League campaign.

Ekitike's absence has been a frustrating setback for Liverpool , with the striker forced to watch from the sidelines while his teammates navigate a demanding fixture schedule.

However, there is growing optimism that the 24-year-old could be approaching the final stages of his recovery, with Iraola offering an encouraging assessment of his rehabilitation.

According to The Telegraph journalist Dominic King , Liverpool's head coach remains hopeful that Ekitike could feature in the club's final two Champions League league-phase fixtures against Inter Milan and Lens .

While the Frenchman's rehabilitation is progressing as expected, Iraola revealed that he remains slightly behind fellow injury absentees Conor Bradley and Giovanni Leoni in his recovery programme.

Speaking about Ekitike's potential return, Iraola confirmed:

"If nothing is going wrong then January is what it should be, yes."

Although the update provides encouragement, Liverpool will understandably be reluctant to rush their forward back into competitive action before he is fully fit.

Ekitike's eventual return would provide a significant boost to Liverpool's attacking options during what promises to be an important second half of the campaign.

The French international has established himself as an exciting attacking talent, offering a combination of intelligent movement, technical ability and a willingness to stretch opposition defences.

His versatility across the frontline also gives Iraola additional tactical flexibility, something Liverpool could benefit from as domestic and European commitments continue to intensify.

With the January fixture schedule approaching, having another recognised attacking option available could prove invaluable.

However, the fact that Bradley and Leoni are currently further ahead in their respective rehabilitation programmes suggests patience will be required.

Liverpool's medical staff will undoubtedly prioritise Ekitike's long-term fitness rather than risk aggravating his injury through a premature return.

The possibility of Ekitike featuring against Inter Milan or Lens gives Liverpool supporters something positive to look towards.

Nevertheless, Iraola's comments suggest that January remains a target rather than a guaranteed return date.

For Liverpool, the priority is ensuring their striker returns in the best possible condition, particularly with the business end of the season approaching.

If his rehabilitation continues without complications, Ekitike could soon provide Iraola with another important attacking weapon as the Reds look to strengthen their position both domestically and in Europe.

articles.title: Women’s World Cup 2035: Where in the UK games will likely take place
articles.summary: World football's premier tournament was last held in the UK in 1966, when England won the men’s tournament
articles.body:
Confirmation that the United Kingdom will stage a World Cup for the first time since 1966 is expected on Monday.

The 2035 Women's World Cup is on course to be co-hosted by England, Northern Ireland, Scotland and Wales, who are the only bidders for the tournament.

A specially arranged virtual Congress of FIFA 's member nations is set to rubber-stamp their hosting.

World football's premier international tournament was last held on these shores in 1966, when England hosted – and won – the men's World Cup.

Noel Mooney, the chief executive of the Football Association of Wales, said: "Wales has been a football nation for 150 years and we have never hosted anything on this scale. World Cup football played here, in front of Welsh children, would change what this game looks like in Wales: in the clubs, in the schools, and in the number of girls who grow up seeing a pathway into it.

"Anyone who has been to a Cymru game knows the atmosphere our supporters create in a stadium. To see that support for the best teams in the world would be something to see. We are looking forward to seeing what happens on Monday."

FIFA's evaluation of the bid, published earlier this month, rated it 4.3 out of five.

Nineteen venues are proposed, with 14 in England, one in Northern Ireland, two in Scotland and two in Wales in a tournament which will feature 48 teams. One of those venues – Old Trafford – has been included in its current guise but any rebuilt stadium is envisaged to be a host.

A further three stadiums could be added – Birmingham's new Powerhouse Stadium, Wrexham's redeveloped Racecourse Ground and a potential new Chelsea stadium – which would take the tournament to 16 cities and 22 stadiums across the four nations.

**To be replaced by the 'new' Old Trafford if completed

articles.title: Title decided, but: See what's at stake in Brasileirão and have your say
articles.summary: The Brasileirão title has already been decided, with Flamengo crowned champions, but the league still has PLENTY of unfinished business.As things stand, two...
articles.body:
The Brasileirão title has already been decided, with Flamengo crowned champions, but the league still has PLENTY of unfinished business.

As things stand, two Libertadores spots and six Sul-Americana spots are still up for grabs.

Meanwhile, only one team has been mathematically relegated. Three more will go down.

Flamengo, Palmeiras and Cruzeiro have already secured their places in the 2027 Libertadores group stage.

Fluminense will also compete in the tournament, but the Rio club is still fighting for the last direct group-stage spot.

As things stand, fifth and sixth place qualify for the Libertadores preliminary rounds. Those positions are currently held by Athletico and Bahia, respectively.

But Atlético-MG (Sul-Americana runners-up), Santos, RB Bragantino and Vasco still have a chance of breaking into the top six.

The Brasileirão can no longer have nine Libertadores qualifying spots (because Atlético-MG finished runners-up in the Sul-Americana).

But as many as eight teams could qualify if Palmeiras win the Libertadores and Grêmio are relegated to Série B.

As things stand, teams finishing seventh through 12th qualify for the 2027 Sul-Americana.

But that could change depending on Palmeiras' Libertadores campaign and Grêmio's fate in the Brasileirão.

For now, Atlético-MG, Santos, RB Bragantino, Vasco, Coritiba and São Paulo occupy the Sul-Americana qualifying places.

If the qualifying cutoff moves from 12th to 14th, for example, Botafogo (13th) and Vitória (14th) would benefit from the extra spots.

But even Internacional and Grêmio (who are in the relegation zone) could still secure a Sul-Americana spot.

With the possibility of Sul-Americana qualification extending to 14th place, several teams will be fighting for a Sul-Americana spot and Série A survival at the same time.

Right now, only Chapecoense have been mathematically relegated.

Remo could go down in this 36th round of fixtures (they visit Athletico).

Rivals Grêmio and Internacional (both on 38 points) are in the relegation zone. Corinthians are 16th with 40. Mirassol (41), Vitória (41) and Botafogo (42) are still at risk.

São Paulo, in 12th place with 44 points, face a small risk. One point would guarantee survival, but 44 points may already be enough.

articles.title: El PSG confirma las peores noticias: Doué se rompe el cruzado
articles.standfirst: El club parisino emitió este domingo un comunicado para confirmar las peores previsiones para el atacante
articles.summary: El club parisino emitió este domingo un comunicado para confirmar las peores previsiones para el atacante
articles.body: El PSG ha confirmado este domingo los peores presagios. Désiré Doué tiene roto el ligamento cruzado anterior de la rodilla derecha según ha confirmado el club parisino en un comunicado. El jugador sufrió esta lesión el sábado durante el partido de Ligue 1 frente al Niza tras abandonar el campo entre lágrimas y someterse a una resonancia magnética. El club ha señalado que el futbolista será operado antes de que finalice noviembre, lo que le hace decir prácticamente adiós al resto de la temporada y le impedirá disputar los cuartos de final de la Nations League contra España en marzo. La baja supone un duro revés para el proyecto de Luis Enrique, que ya había perdido a Kvaratskhelia por la misma dolencia en octubre ante el Barcelona y ahora se queda sin otro titular clave en el doblete reciente de Champions. Doué había asumido mayor protagonismo ofensivo tras la ausencia del extremo georgiano, acumulando participación directa en diez goles en quince encuentros entre todas las competiciones. Ante este escenario, el campeón de Europa deberá mover piezas y contar con Ferran Torres y Ousmane Dembélé en esa posición para sostener su ataque en los próximos compromisos. Asimismo, la entidad parisina, que inicialmente descartaba acudir al mercado invernal tras la lesión de Kvaratskhelia, podría replantearse fichar en enero para compensar la falta de efectivos de primer nivel.

articles.title: Xabi Alonso on the brink? Chelsea boss warned sack decision is looming after 'disgusting' Leeds humiliation
articles.summary: Xabi Alonso is fighting to save his job at Stamford Bridge after a disastrous run of form culminated in a humiliating home defeat. The Spaniard has been warn...
articles.body:
Xabi Alonso is fighting to save his job at Stamford Bridge after a disastrous run of form culminated in a humiliating home defeat. The Spaniard has been warned that his tenure in west London could be cut short unless he orchestrates an immediate and dramatic turnaround in both results and performances.

Stamford Bridge turns on Alonso during heavy defeat

Stamford Bridge descended into frustration on Saturday as Chelsea collapsed to a 4-1 loss against Leeds . That setback followed a 1-0 defeat at struggling Sunderland two weeks earlier and an uncommon home loss to rivals Tottenham.

Supporters voiced their anger, directing chants of "you don't know what you're doing" at the dugout when Malo Gusto was introduced. While an understanding exists that his methods require time to settle, Alonso's substitutions have repeatedly drawn scrutiny.

Cundy delivers blunt verdict on 'disgusting' display

Former Chelsea player Jason Cundy delivered a scathing verdict on talkSPORT after the Leeds collapse, warning a change beckons without an instant response.

"We are rotten. We were so bad, it was so bad… I'm in disbelief at what I've just witnessed," Cundy said. "That was a worrying performance, worrying. If that carries on, Alonso won't keep his job, I'm telling you that for nothing."

Highlighting consecutive losses to struggling Sunderland and Leeds, he condemned the capitulation. "You can't do what you did against Sunderland, you can't do what you did against Leeds today and lose those two games," he added. "We were disgusting today, absolutely disgusting, I'm still trying to find the words… as every minute ticked by, we got worse, and Leeds got better."

Growing gap to Arsenal sparks bottom-half concerns

After 11 Premier League games, Chelsea sit eighth and already trail leaders Arsenal by 12 points. The regression has left Cundy questioning where the club will finish.

"It's almost disbelief at how bad we were, seriously, I'm not even joking. I'm worried… I'm worried about how this season is going to go," Cundy admitted. "Genuinely now, I'm worried… I am worried about what this season looks like for us."

He added: "I'm being completely honest here, I don't know whether we're going to finish… we look like bottom half fodder, easily bottom half fodder ... anyone could've beaten us, we were that bad. I'm really struggling to work out how we could've been that bad."

Crucial tests against struggling rivals await

Alonso faces an immediate test with consecutive games against teams near the foot of the table. Chelsea visit struggling Nottingham Forest next weekend before hosting relegation-threatened Crystal Palace a week later. Amid mounting pressure, anything short of two victories could prove fatal for his prospects.

articles.title: Jürgen Klopp ‘happy’ with Germany drawing Belgium in the Nations League
articles.summary: The Germans face a good test in the knockout round of the Nations League
articles.body:
After strong showing in the UEFA Nations League, Jürgen Klopp led Germany to the quarterfinals where they will face Belgium. The 59-year-old coach said he's happy with the draw and profiled his team's opponents.

"I'm happy with the draw. I'm looking forward to facing Belgium. They're a strong opponent, and they also have a new manager," Klopp said (as captured by X account @iMiaSanMia ). "They had a great Nations League campaign, and I know several of their players very well. Kevin De Bruyne is one of the greatest players the Premier League has ever seen. And he's still good – unfortunately. We're fully aware that we're right at the beginning of a development process. We want to carry this positive atmosphere forward, but there's still a lot of work to do."

The last time the two sides met in 2023, Belgium won 3-2 which was their first victory over the Germans since 1954. Despite that fact, Germany always beat Belgium in competitive matches.

articles.title: Did CJ Carr and KVA hint at their Notre Dame future’s post-SMU?
articles.summary: Following Notre Dame’s win over SMU, stars CJ Carr and Kyngstonn Viliamu-Asa did something that could hint towards their NFL futures.
articles.body:
It was a great Senior Day for Notre Dame football, as it defeated SMU 24-3 as they march closer and closer to securing a bid for the College Football Playoff .

Obviously, we can't help but think about the future for the Irish, the near and far as well. While we know that every senior that was honored last night has exhausted their eligibility, there are plenty of others that could have taken their last snaps in the Blue and Gold.

Following the game, Pete Sampson shared on social media that quarterback CJ Carr and linebacker Kyngstonn Viliamu-Asa stayed behind to take a picture together. He said to make of that what you will, and so I think that both of them have played their last game for Notre Dame.

Look, we all want them to come back, but when you are considering as a first-round NFL draft prospect, you have to go. Football only lasts so long, the shortest career among major professional sports, as the window to earn more is cut short the later you enter the league. If Carr and KVA did come back, the Irish could be national title favorites.

However, I could be totally wrong, and they were just taking a photo to really remember the season. We'll find out soon, hopefully sometime late in January following a CFP title.

articles.title: WSL: Arsenal draw again at home, Man Utd leave it late to beat Birmingham and Charlton earn first point of season
articles.summary: Arsenal drew their sixth successive home WSL game against West Ham; Man Utd left it late to beat Birmingham as their improvement continues; Charlton earned their first point of the season against Aston Villa; a horror own goal saw Brighton beat Everton; Man City also lost at home to Spurs
articles.body:
The Hammers avoided defeat to the Gunners for the first time to pile the pressure on Renee Slegers and her side, who now have just 15 points after 11 games and sit in sixth.

Arsenal had 22 shots in total, with 67 per cent possession, but did not create one big chance throughout.

The best chance of the game came through substitute Kyra Cooney-Cross when her shot struck the post following a big deflection.

But, overall, it was another tepid display in front of the home crowd, and those in red did not do enough to finally emerge with three points.

The well-deserved point for West Ham takes them above Liverpool into 12th.

Manchester United left it very late to claim a 2-1 victory over Birmingham.

Geum-Min Lee put struggling Birmingham in front in only the fourth minute and United struggled to create clear-cut chances, while Phallon Tullis-Joyce made a couple of crucial saves.

The visitors finally found the breakthrough 10 minutes from time through Elisabeth Terland, and Simi Awujo broke Birmingham hearts with a header four minutes into added time.

Bottom-side Charlton claimed their first point of the season at the 11th time of asking with a 1-1 draw against Aston Villa.

Keira Flannery put Charlton ahead with a first-half penalty but Lucy Parker pulled Villa level 19 minutes from time.

An early own goal scored by Maz Pacheco saw struggling Everton fall to a 1-0 defeat at home to Brighton.

Earlier on Sunday, Manchester City saw their 17-game winning league run at the Joie Stadium come to an end with a 3-1 defeat to Tottenham.

Slegers takes responsibility after another home draw

Renee Slegers speaking after Arsenal's 0-0 draw with West Ham on whether she is considering her future:

"I love the club. I'm very passionate about this group of players, we're going through a very difficult time, and I take my responsibilities because the results haven't been good enough.

"In the second half we are chasing again but we're not creating good enough chances to the final third, from all phases, and the way we get there, it's not the Arsenal standard and we need to do that better. But I take my responsibilities in my role.

"That [fans booing] is on us and that's our responsibility. That it's so quiet in the stadium because we don't inspire enough. We don't bring enough energy.

"I think, about the fans, because it's cold and they want to see good football and get inspired today and that's not what we did. And at the end of the day, that's my responsibility.

"That doesn't feel good. The fans booing at the end, they care and they want more from this team, which the group is determined to turn things around.

"It's very tough for the players and the players that have been at Arsenal for longer, or even the players that came last year. No one has gone through this ever with Arsenal.

"The group has been great. They've been very good in the situation but, of course, it's the last one of the block and frustration is expressed, which I don't think is a bad thing because we shouldn't be accepting this."

articles.title: Liverpool vs Man Utd: Was red card for Leny Yoro in Premier League the correct decision?
articles.summary: Leny Yoro's red card after eight minutes changed Liverpool v Manchester United - did officials make the correct call?
articles.body:
Leny Yoro's eighth-minute red card was a pivotal moment early in Mauricio Pochettino's first game as Manchester United boss.

It handed Liverpool the initiative at Anfield, and Andoni Iraola's players took advantage by scoring two goals in quick succession.

Was there a case for the video assistant referee (VAR) to suggest it should be downgraded to a yellow?

Let's take a look at the incident, and what a referee takes into account before showing a red for denying an obvious goalscoring opportunity.

What happened and what will the officials have taken into consideration?

Ronald Araujo played a long ball upfield for Alexander Isak to run on to.

Isak took a touch, before Yoro bundled into the back of the Sweden international and brought him down.

Referee Sam Barrott did not hesitate, giving the foul and sending off Yoro.

Was there doubt that Isak would have taken control of the ball? If so, it should only be a caution.

There are four key considerations for denying an obvious goalscoring opportunity:

distance between the offence and the goal

likelihood of keeping or gaining control of the ball

location and number of defenders and attackers

As Isak was running directly towards goal in a central position, and there was no covering defender, three of the factors were satisfied.

The question is about the "likelihood of keeping or gaining control of the ball".

The Liverpool striker took a heavy touch, which moved the ball a few yards ahead of him.

The touch came before contact from Yoro, so there is no case that the challenge caused Isak to over-run the ball.

The referee and the VAR, John Brooks, must therefore assess whether Isak would definitely have got to the ball ahead of Senne Lammens. And that if he had, it would have been a good scoring chance.

If there is any doubt, then it should not be a red card.

It is a borderline case, and as such the VAR would not be expected to intervene for a clear and obvious error.

Likewise, if the referee had shown a yellow the VAR would not get involved.

Former Liverpool and England midfielder Danny Murphy, who is a pundit on Sunday's Match of the Day, said there was "no doubt" about the red card.

Former Manchester United defender Gary Neville also agreed with the decision.

"Leny Yoro has to cover and he doesn't," Neville said on Sky Sports. "He reacts late and his anticipation is poor.

"It's so clumsy from Yoro. It's naivety, he just needs to get off the pitch. You're not going to get that turned around, no chance."

But for Liverpool boss Iraola the decision is not up for debate.

"I think he's the last man, no?" he said. "It's a clear foul and a red card, yes?

Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes felt it should not have been a red card and said the decision had a detrimental impact on the game.

"It's one that needs to be looked at," Fernandes told Sky Sports.

"We have far too many meetings with the referees for this to happen to us again. The last one against Chelsea [when Lisandro Martinez was sent off], you can give it as a red card and it was probably a second yellow also. Today, you can't give a red card.

"It's very clear they show us if the player is not in control of the ball, it's never a red card.

"Isak kicks the ball forward, the ball goes into the hands of Senne. Isak has got no control of the ball, he has no chance to get on the ball. He puts his leg across to try to get some advantage from Leny. I can understand the fall, but it's never a red card.

"There are too many referees on the pitch and too many on VAR taking so long to see to make a mistake like this that can change the game.

"It's not because of them we conceded the goal from the free-kick, but it changes the game completely."

Pochettino, meanwhile, was frustrated by what he perceived as inconsistency in the decision-making of the officials.

The former Tottenham and Chelsea boss felt his new team should have been awarded a penalty moments before Yoro was sent off, after Jeremy Jacquet went shoulder to shoulder with Bryan Mbeumo.

"It's difficult to accept that because it was a foul under my view and for me was a penalty," Pochettino told Match of the Day.

"Look how everything changes if that action was a red card and a foul, I think we need to review. When I played football that situation is normal. The action against Mbeumo, if that [Yoro foul on Isak] was a red card then that was a penalty."

There have been a couple of very similar cases this season.

Brighton's Pascal Struijk was sent off at Sunderland through a VAR review after he brought down Wilson Isidor.

The Seagulls successfully appealed against that red card on the grounds that there was clear doubt that Isidor would have taken control of the ball before it ran through to goalkeeper Bart Verbruggen.

Could Manchester United appeal against Yoro's red card? There's nothing to lose by doing so.

Despite the Football Association regulatory commission unanimously ruling the Struijk red card was wrong, the Premier League's key match incidents panel voted the VAR intervention was a correct call on a split 3-2 vote.

Ipswich's Issa Diop avoided a VAR red card for a foul on James McAtee against Nottingham Forest, when the referee disagreed with the video official, and believed there was a covering defender. Forest boss Oliver Glasner was adamant it had been a clear goalscoring opportunity.

It was the same referee, Thomas Bramall, for both of those incidents.

That shows just how subjective such decisions can be. It is often rare to get a real consensus.

Yoro can count himself a little unfortunate to get the red card.

articles.title: AP College Football Poll 2026 Week 13 Rankings Released with Top Risers and Fallers
articles.summary: The newest Associated Press Top 25 poll lays bare how rough Saturday was for the Big Ten.
articles.body:
The newest Associated Press Top 25 poll lays bare how rough Saturday was for the Big Ten.

Having gained some ground, Ohio State is back down in 25th after losing 31-28 to Nebraska. UCLA's status as a top five team is gone with the Bruins tasting defeat for the first time. Indiana, meanwhile, could be slipping toward the College Football Playoff bubble thanks to a 27-24 overtime loss to Washington.

The Hoosiers' misfortune opened the door for Wake Forest to occupy its highest-ever position (No. 8) in the AP poll.

The Demon Deacons continued their offensive blitz, dropping 50-plus points for the third time in four games.

Gio Lopez went 17-of-22 for 324 yards and two touchdowns through the air, while Deuce Lawrence and Ty Clark III combined to run for 203 yards and three scores. They all helped Wake take a 29-0 lead in the first half.

Wake Forest will get a rematch against Miami in the ACC title game. If the Demon Deacons prevail and own a 12-1 record, they'll have a strong case to earn a first-round bye in the playoff.

That's a luxury UCLA might've thrown away thanks to its flat performance against Michigan. The Bruins finished with 296 yards of offense and didn't score their first touchdown until there were 10 seconds left in regulation.

The night was even more costly as backup quarterback Ty Dieffenbach suffered an injury , forcing third-stringer Madden Iamaleava to step up in the first overtime period.

UCLA looked like a playoff lock when it was sitting on a perfect 10-0 record. Now, there's a chance the Bruins could miss the CFP altogether because their resume would take a big hit if they close the season with back-to-back defeats.

Indiana, meanwhile, no longer controls its destiny in the Big Ten title race. On top of beating Purdue, the Hoosiers need results to break in their favor on Thanksgiving weekend to book a trip to Indianapolis.

Will the CFP selection committee be swayed by a 10-2 Indiana that didn't win the conference? Previous installments of the playoff rankings would suggest not .

Michigan, Ohio State and Indiana winning national championships led many to wonder whether the Big Ten had supplanted the SEC as the best football conference. This year, the Big Ten is facing a scenario where it may have just one representative in the playoff.

Expansion to 24 teams probably can't come soon enough for B1G commissioner Tony Petitti.

articles.title: El Girona da una alegría a Montilivi
articles.standfirst: Los de Quique Álvarez ganan, por primera vez en su casa, a un rival directo
articles.summary: Los de Quique Álvarez ganan, por primera vez en su casa, a un rival directo
articles.body: El Girona ganó al Eibar, otro de los equipos que estará seguro luchando por el ascenso hasta el final de la temporada (2-1). Los catalanes se adelantaron con un tanto de Vanat, que aprovechó un toque de Pyshchur para empujar el balón a placer (36’), pero los guipuzcoanos empataron después de una acción polémica en la que el VAR intervino en un empujón de Mate dentro del área que el árbitro no había decretado como falta. Mada empató (44’) y Unai Hernández, que controló el esférico en el segundo palo y superó Magunagoitia, estableció el 2-1 definitivo pese al asedio final, y lógico, de un Eibar que inquietó poco en general a un buen Gazzaniga. La primera hora del partido fue plana y aburrida. El Girona no sabía como atacar el bloque bajo bien ordenado del Eibar, mientras que los armeros lo fiaban todo a la recuperación y la transición veloz con Adu Ares, Guruzeta y compañía como estiletes. Pyshchur, como siempre muy activo, generó estrés a la defensa visitante hasta los catalanes pudieron avanzarse, precisamente, con dos jugadores ucranianos como protagonistas. Asprilla vio muy bien el desmarque del gigante de hielo, que puso la punta de la bota para picar ante la salida de Magunagoitia y habilitar a Vanat, su compatriota, para que empujará a gol y abriera la lata (36’). Los de Quique Álvarez tenían el partido donde lo querían hasta que el VAR rasgó el guion en una jugada dudosa en la que Mate empujó -levemente o no- a Magunazelaia. Morilla Turrión no vio falta pero sí López Toca desde Las Rozas dando a Mada la opción de empatar (44’). Antes del descanso, Pyshchur estrelló un remate a la base del palo izquierdo del Eibar (45+2’), una acción que podía haber cambiado otra vez el signo de un partido que se calentó con la grada de Montilivi indignada desde el empate. El segundo acto empezó con Eibar avisando seriamente después que Martón viera muy bien el desmarque de Álvaro Rodríguez, que había hecho una gran diagonal. El lateral no pudo superar Gazzaniga, que salió algo lento pero achicó espacios como nadie para evitar el gol (51’). Poco después, en una jugada aislada, Vanat recibió fuera de su zona, escorado a la derecha pero recortó bien a su marcador para hacer un centro medido al segundo palo donde llegaba Unai Hernández. El jugador cedido por el Al-Ittihad controló con maestría el esférico y remató cruzado ante Magunagoitia para hacer el 2-1 (59’). Quedaba mucho tiempo, pero el Eibar solo inquietó a través de Martón, que obligó a Gazzaniga a estirarse para poner una mano salvadora (68’) y en algún centro sin dueño ya con el propio Martón y Bautista en el campo.

articles.title: Liverpool 4-0 Man Utd: Gary Neville on Matthijs de Ligt selection and 'negligent' Red Devils
articles.summary: Manchester United were thrashed 4-0 by Liverpool in Mauricio Pochettino's first game as head coach after Leny Yoro's eighth-minute red card; Red Devils have conceded 34 goals in all competitions this season - the most by any side in Europe's major leagues
articles.body:
Liverpool ran riot after Leny Yoro's eighth-minute red card at Anfield as goals from Dominik Szoboszlai, Florian Wirtz, Rio Ngumoha and Victor Munoz ensured Mauricio Pochettino suffered a horror start to his Manchester United tenure.

United have now conceded 34 goals in all competitions this term. It is the highest total of any side across Europe's top-five leagues. The result keeps them second from bottom in the Premier League.

"It's negligent," said Sky Sports pundit Neville.

"The negligence is not bringing in defenders in the transfer window, because we've seen this for two or three years."

Pochettino made the decision to hand Matthijs de Ligt his first Premier League start in 357 days at Anfield but the Netherlands international was partly at fault for the opening goal and endured a torrid evening along with the rest of United's defenders.

Watching back the opener, when De Ligt misjudged a high ball, Neville said: "The minute that De Ligt makes that run in that channel, Yoro has to come across within 10 metres of him, and [Diogo] Dalot has to come across. This is so bad from Yoro and Dalot.

"De Lift makes a right mess of it. He can't believe it though, De Ligt. He's played centre-half before. He can't believe Yoro's not there. Then Yoro makes contact and it's clumsy.

"Honestly. You can't get worse that that.

"You've got a back four who are looking after their own jobs, they're in fear.

"De Ligt and [Lisandro] Martinez have dropped off, Dalot's not coming quickly enough.

"It's a mess because of the fact they've got no confidence and haven't got the ability to play out there at Anfield in a game against Liverpool."

Neville 'very surprised' by De Ligt call

Neville was baffled by Pochettino's decision to start De Ligt, who was similarly poor when returning from injury in last month's 4-1 loss to Como in the Champions League.

"We were in the trucks over in the compound and when the team came through straight away we were very surprised," added Neville.

"I just didn't think Manchester United would win, and I thought they would concede lots of goals and make mistakes.

"Maybe the options on the bench aren't brilliant either, but it's really desperate and it's tiring watching them.

"Mauricio Pochettino's options are not great, but I didn't get De Ligt.

"Having been out for a year myself, it's really difficult to come back into a game like that.

"I'm not saying that you can't, but as a centre-back getting your bearings… You saw him in Como, he was all over the place in Como.

"It's almost like you don't know what's happening.

"I found that coming back into it when I was 32, he's obviously more experienced as well.

"I was very surprised he played but then the others haven't been doing great either."

United's total of eight points after 11 games is their lowest at this stage of a season since the 1972/73 campaign.

"You wonder how low it can get, but this is as low as it's been in 54 years," added Neville.

"A few weeks ago against Fulham, I said it's the worst 40 minutes or 30 minutes I've seen in my lifetime.

"At the time people said that was maybe a bit too much, but this is actually the worst Manchester United have ever been in 54 years. It's a fact.

"The worst defensive team in Europe, second bottom in the league, they've never started this badly."

He added: "I would have started with Harry Maguire today. Manchester United's best back four - and I think we're informed enough to know, we've watched these lads for two or three years - is [Luke] Shaw, Dalot, Maguire and Martinez.

"Now, it's a poor back four, let me be really clear. But it is Manchester United's best back four.

"Now, if you can get that back four out on the pitch, it does win games, against Liverpool last year, it does win games against City and Arsenal, it can compete slightly.

"But that back four that started today, and the one that finished against Villa a few weeks ago of [Noussair] Mazraoui, [Patrick] Dorgu, Yoro, and [Ayden] Heaven - that will get you relegated, that's a fact."
